greetings: Energy lashes out around your hands climbing along your arm in an effort to engulf your body. A high pitched screech wails in your mind.
You reach down and pickup the mask. You nearly drop it when you see two eyes staring from the eyeholes. An instant later they are gone.
As your hand falls on the mask the surface ripples and voice calls to you "Put it on. Yes, we will be as one. Wear it."
As you pickup the mask you have an overwhelming urge to put it on. Everything looks so much more vibrant through the eyeholes.

The mask slips onto your face, and feels wet. Tendrils of energy loop into your cheeks and a purple hue covers your eyes for a brief moment. The world swims and your consciousness enhances. The smell of burned flesh fills your nostrils.
"Am I not comfortable?" The flesh on your face shifts and contorts. "How about now?"
A man's voice fills your head. "Do you hear voices? I do. I cannot escape them!"
The wretched mask slips over your head and for a moment you wonder... will it ever come off?
A man's voice bellows "Ahhhh! GET OUT OF MY HEAD!"
As the mask falls into place you see Virindi... everywhere. The faces melt into nothingness after a few panicked moments.
A man's voice screams "The pain! The pain!"

Your breath quickens and a pain grows in your chest. Your head begins to hum and the world begins to close in upon you ever tighter. Claustrophobia clutches you in vice-like grip. The mask tightens on your skull threatening to crush it.
Your vision clouds. You are standing in a doorway watching a woman cradle a small child. She appears to be weeping. You look at your ruined, clawed hand and begin to weep yourself.
As you wear the mask your vision fails you and it feels like egg yolks begin to run down your face.
Your vision clouds. Magical energy crackles all around you as a deafening hum pervades the air. You feel a sense of satisfaction as you stare into the shocked and widening eyes of Gaerlan.
Beside you the portal swirls. You force the energy ever outwards driving it into the very core of the citadel below you. Your flesh sloughs off, and your robe falls to the ground. Human once more.
The explosions begin. You knew they would, a flash of brilliant white light ruins the vision in your right eye and you stumble. The sound of your magic and the whir of the portal all that are left.
Your breathing becomes labored. There is no pain. You hear a woman's voice, soft and loving. "Candeth... Candeth..." The sound of a small child's laughter fills your head. You smile.
Darkness clouds your vision. You hear water dripping and smell blood. A voice invades your mind and pervades your thoughts "Puppet, Reports are strong today. Puppet assimilates well."
You have a strange thought. "Power it could be ours again."
As you don the shell of Martine, you are overcome by the feeling of slugs crawling all over your face for a moment, until the mask slips into place, and all is well.
You feel the flesh of your face searing becoming one with the mask.
You feel an irresistable urge to limp.
You feel alone in the world. All around you are enemies. They will not help you quell the renegades. These Isparian meatlings must be destroyed.
As you place the mask on your face tendrils of energy reach into the recesses of your mind sqeezing down. The eye sockets of the mask blink open and closed in quick succession.
For a moment you think of home and family, then the memories fade into an array of abstract analysis, devoid of soul.
Your thoughts stray to Elysa, no Melanay, Elysa, no Melanay.
As your thoughts stray to Asheron you think of home and the wife and child you have lost. You have an urge to scream.
A warm feeling of home and hearth fills your mind. You see a child playing at your feet... and then the sensation fades.
A man's voice says, "Eyes in the dark."
A man's voice says, "Two moons circle."
A man's voice says, "Am I not a man? Correction. Are we not men?"
The ghostly image of a fallen Tusker, its skull exploded open from the inside, appears in front of you. A smile creeps onto your face and then the image disappears.

A mosswart with outstretched arms, screaming in what appears to be pain, dangles before you. Its screaming becomes ragged and finally ceases as its head drops down to its chest and mosswart disappears.
The face of the enemy appears before you. He speaks consoling words, but your mind fills with hate as you struggle to attack this man... and then the feeling fades.
Your mind is flooded with the sights and sounds of a bustling port and a melancholy feeling overpowers your thoughts, but the vision soon fades.

A small boy looks at you without fear. You had meant to kill him. Arrita's giggles fill your head as you look at the tattered letter in your hand. Melanay's kisses and gentle smile come to mind and you stand. "Come Borelean it is time to make amends."
Screeches, howls, hums and unearthly sounds of wet fingers running along crystal pervade your mind a pulsing thrum throbs within. The singularity calls to you.
You squeal trapped in a cell devoid of light. You are but a fraction when once you were a whole. You have a feeling you had never had before. Loss.
Your sanity shatters like a crystal goblet.
The calming chimes of the singularity tug at the back of your mind and your consciousness threatens to slip away.
He stands before you and offers the way home. You hesitate a moment and you think his offer is sound.

As the magic coalesces and tears through Asheron's chest you smile broadly thinking now you will have Elysa for your own. But the betrayal is at hand when your mind clears and your conscience becomes heavy.
An arrow slices through your throat. Rocks pelt against your head and body. People beat your body bloody. You have become the slayer of hope.
Asheron quells the ravages in your mind. You begin to think clearer as if a great weight has been lifted from your mind.
A man's voice says, "As you have done for me, I now return the favor." Asheron's wounds close and he looks upon you.
The feeling of intense claustrophobia lifts as you slip that disgusting shell from your head.
A tinny voice calls out, "Where are you putting me? I liked it there."
A tinny voice calls out, "No! Put me back!"
A tinny voice calls out, "Don't leave me alone. I can't stand to be alone."
When you remove the mask, the voices in your head decrease to the normal level.
The mask slips from your skull with a sickeningly slick sound.
As you pull the mask from your head the flesh threatens to come with it.
The mask refuses to give up its grip on your skull for a moment.
A sound of Virindi holding a conversation in your head sounds as you peel the mask from your face.
As you try to pull the mask from your face the eye sockets and mouth close off choking you near to death.
Martine arrives and surveys the destroyed crystal.
You have done well. This is our first assault against Gaerlan. I...
Martine pauses and looks to the floor. He breathes a heavy sigh and then looks at all the warriors, mages and archers assembled.
I was wrong. Moreover, I failed in bringing the peace for which I yearned. My desires to lead you, to kill Asheron, the harm I brought to Elysa to all of you, all results of Gaerlan's poison words.

Gaerlan appeared in my holding on Marae Lassel as I set the portals to the island here on Dereth. It was an unintentional breach of a Virindi shield that surrounds the Empyrean in portal space that freed him from his stasis. Upon seeing him I had intended to kill him, but he groveled well.
He offered me a gift in exchange for his life. My one true desire. My heart's true wish. A way home. The same way home that he now taunts us with. Ispar...

I believed him, I sheltered him, and now he has betrayed me. I have read what he has written, his diary, and his reports. They inspired me to visit a larger area of Auberean, looking for evidence of the portal destination from the Olthoi world.

My time there was brief, for the lands there are covered in blight, fungus, and Olthoi. They cluster together on the land and in cavernous burrows beneath the golden cities of the Yalain. Smaller winged Olthoi fill the sky. The fliers are too small to carry their larger cousins, and look too fragile to embark across the sea, I think they are of no true threat...now.

I made my way to Knorr. The Lyceum where Asheron taught his pupils. I searched for evidence of his magic at the place where the Olthoi invaded this world. It is a trick that I learned, when I closed the portals from Ispar to Dereth. I expected to find that it was Asheron's magic that was left, but I found something else...
I found traces of Gaerlan's magic at the arrival point. It was Gaerlan...his folly, his miscalculation. He moved the portal from their world, when he tried to trap Asheron there. He did not close it.
The Yalaini have held Asheron accountable for this folly and made him a criminal, even though he has saved his race...saved our race. And I meant to kill him...
Martine pauses and looks at the assembled crowd.

A little boy, a little prince, came to me. He asked me why I tried to kill his uncle. I could not find an answer to his question. I searched within myself to find one, to tell him that Asheron had caused me all of this pain. But Asheron did not bring this upon me. Alayne sold me to the Mosswarts, and the Virindi.

It was curiosity, and an explorer's nature, that made me use the portal to Dereth. We all, made the choice to come here, as others do every day on Ispar. The portals call to us, but it is in our nature to seek something different and new.
Asheron lives, and with his assistance we will overcome Gaerlan, bring his fortress down, and right what has been made wrong with Dereth.
Martine's voice takes on a very deep and guttural tone.

Gaerlan's power is drawn from these crystals that sap the mana from the ley lines beneath Dereth. A barrier surrounds his citadel. This barrier is impenetrable as far as I can discern. I cannot circumvent it by the magical means that I know. We must continue our efforts and destroy these crystals.

Asheron is at work in his Castle, with Elysa. They are divining the locations of these caverns so that you might have access to the crystals. You will be informed when they have found the second, third and fourth. I will be preparing...
I intend to bring the citadel down. I have unfinished business with Gaerlan.
Gaerlan will have his reckoning!
Until next we meet...
Goodbye
Martine surveys the area.

A decisive victory. Gaerlan will not allow us to seize his power passively. There will be more resistance as we edge closer to taking his seat of power. New pitfalls will appear, and we must all be prepared.
With this second crystal shattered we have drawn much attention to our efforts. He will surely become desperate soon.

Asheron has informed me that he has noticed a horrible disturbance and fluctuation in the flow of mana beneath the fallen city of Yanshi. Elysa has sent a contingent of her Royal Guard around the city and is sending her most learned scholar to assist in the study of what transpires there.
Martine lets out a soft laugh.

It is possible that something has gone terribly wrong for Gaerlan already, but the result of this error could have larger implications for the world. Asheron has thus placed the discovery of these chambers upon me. I will inform you when the next has been found and furnish you with a way into the heart of the cistern.
Martine looks as though he will leave for moment, then he examines the gathered populace.

In my discussion with Asheron I learned something of importance. The Empyrean that are still trapped in portal space are sealed from him. He cannot see any of them. For the past several years he has struggled to pierce a veil that was put in place by the Virindi.

When the lifestones were created they did indeed have a dual purpose. They anchored our souls and bodies to this world, circumventing a death that was not natural. They were once the beacons that the Yalaini used to guide their ships. Powerful navigational devices would drive massive stone structures and great ships through the air to these waypoints.

When Elysa, and the other humans, emerged from the Olthoi caves victorious over the True Queen, Asheron altered the lifestones composition. What Gaerlan told me is true. The lifestones do siphon energy from us, feeding it to the Empyreans in portal space. A lifeline of sorts. Our sacrifice keeps an entire race alive in the whirl of portal space.

Asheron is a man that holds duty, above his own well being. He feels ultimately responsible for bringing us to this strange world and watches over us as best he can. It is also true that he feels as though he must aid his fellows, trapped there in the world between worlds. But we, have become his primary concern. Though one day he still hopes to free his people.

Asheron thought I held a key to freeing them, he thought that I had been beyond that wall deep within portal space. It was luck though and nothing more. My connection to the singularity through my symbiotic virindi was limited and dissipated quickly as I drove it out and fell into madness.
This news was a blow to him.
Martine shakes his head gently.
So much wasted time focusing my rage on him. So many wasted hours trying to find a way to destroy him, when in truth he only wanted to help me, help all of us.
The penitent man is humbled in the midst of a greater presence, not indignant.
I have much to atone for.
Martine arrives and surveys the devastation.
A battle well fought, and a hard victory wrested from the jaws of defeat. We are closer to Gaerlan's destruction.
We have done well. I thank you for the chance you have given me. Soon we shall hold this world as our own.
One more crystal waits. Buried in the earth, feeding from the mana. Giving him raw energy to command.
Martine pauses and adjusts his mask.
Not as good a fit as it once was.
Martine chuckles.

Elysa told me that her scholar has reported on the situation in Yanshi. Something is growing there, within the temple that Gaerlan used to sacrifice his fallen generals. Odd magical fluctuations and elemental storms have been seen sprouting up in the area of the great stone there.

Asheron is still concerned that the flow of mana has not righted itself even though we have destroyed these active crystals. His concern is that the mana flows have been redirected once more, to an area even deeper beneath Dereth than he thought possible.
He has not stated it openly, but I believe he feels that if this continues, it will hollow the land to a point where it can no longer support its own weight. Crumbling upon itself like a hollow void.
We must act quickly. There is no time to waste. My summons will come as quickly as I can discern the location of the final crystal.
Martine smiles at the people.
I am, Sir Candeth Martine.

Your blood, your sacrifice and your efforts have not gone unnoticed. It is time now that we make our final assault on Gaerlan. Once the base of this crystal is destroyed, I shall ascend to his citadel and destroy the navigation devices. This will cause the citadel to fall to ground, and then we shall take the fight into his home.

But before this, you must know that Asheron and Elysa have discovered the source of the continued entropy of the ley lines. In the place where Gaerlan combined the elemental lords a new elemental is growing. One with complete sentience.
It understands what it does, and means to live its life. We will need to prepare for battle against this creature as well, lest we defeat Gaerlan only to fall to another foe.
Asheron remains resolute in his study of the entity and will afford us with details when he can.
When the time is right I will alert you all of my attack. I wish you to witness my atonement. I will summon portals in my Retreat, the base of this crystal and  the capital cities.
I will make amends for my transgressions.
At Dryreach a portal into the Heart of the Lightning Cistern has opened.
Hee hee hee!
quest: There is nothing more you can do for me. Take your leave.
What is this? Yes...
%n's voice becomes tinny, altering between a deep human voice and distant alien tin voice.
I remember this time well. I was a puppet then, nothing more than an untrained mind with an incomprehensible amount of power. Untapped, raw...
It was during this time, taken from my home, stripped of the woman and child that I loved more than life itself, betrayed by my closest friend...that I decided HE must die.
And now I have succeeded.
%n begins to laugh, softly at first, the human voice most prevalent, then the tinny high-pitched laugh joins his human voice. The laugh grows into a maniacal twist of rage and alien sounds.
Thank you for showing me once again the meaning of my life.
%n sobs.
How I loved her. I miss her so. But look what I have done, what I have become. So many people dead by my hands, and the true savior of this world...dead.
What have I done? How could I have been duped in this way? Read this.
You may need to have it translated if you cannot understand Yalaini writing. But it is important you know.
So much supposition now cleared. I see the truth for the first time.
A tear falls from beneath Martine's mask and lands upon the letter.
How often I sat and wept over this letter that she would never read. Now I weep that if I can see her again I would not be the same man.
Thank you. You have helped me realize that there is still much to do. I must make amends. Go now, please.

greetings: I remember this spear well. Long ago, before Palenqual appeared to show us the true way to create the weapons of life, I carved this spear to be wed to a figurine of Tonk. Together, ths two would realize their vital potential, creating a living spear fit for the finest of our warriors.

I gifted my dear friend Tanua with it, in the night before he left the safety of Timaru to persuade the Hea against their vile pact with the Virindi. I cannot know how he fared, for he never returned to us. If you now have only this part of his weapon, it can only mean that the Hea have betrayed us once more. Please take this back--the sight of it only stirs memories of pain.

I remember this figurine well. Long ago, before Palenqual appeared to show us the true way to create the weapons of life, I molded this figurine to be wed to a spear carved with care. Together the two would realize their vital potential, creating a living spear fit for the finest of our warriors.

I remember this taiaha well. Long ago, before Palenqual appeared to show us the true way to create the weapons of life, I carefully carved a spear to be wed to a figuine of Tonk. Together the two would realize their vital potential, creating a spear fit for the finest of our warriors.

I gifted my dear friend Tanua with it, in the night before he left the safety of Timaru to persuade the Hea against their vile pact with the Virindi. I cannot know how he fared, for he never returned to us. If you now have possession of his weapon, it can only mean that the Hea have betrayed us once more. Please take this back--the sight of it only stirs memories of pain.

I'm sorry, friend, but this totem is obviously of Hea craftmanship. See its inferior carving? The totems I am seeking to restore to my people are made of greenstone, opal, and obsidian. And further--even though the Hea have demeaned themselves by stealing from us, I cannot accept something that belongs to them. You should take this to Aun Hareltah--our Tah will know what to do with it.
quest: Good to see you again! You and other adventurers have helped me regain a sufficient number of our totems. From now on, you may keep any more of our totems that you might find on the Hea.

Aun Shimauri tells you, Thank you, %s, friend of the Aun. You are continually proving your loyalty to us. You may keep this for your own use, and of course, Aun Kerehanua would be happy to greet you in Palenqual's Caverns should you wish to purchase another weapon from him.

Wharu take the Hea! They have stolen our precious totems. If you come across any Hea, you may dispatch them with the Aun's blessings. And if you should find one of our totems on them, bring it to me and I shall confide some of our secrets to you.

We alone among the Tonk have been blessed by Palenqual. In her wrath against Wharu, she has given us the weapons that live to fight against him. Find one of our totems on the Hea, and I will reward you with the friendship of the Aun.

Thank you, traveler. You have proven your friendship to the Aun. Now...Curses on the Hea and their thieving ways! If they had not stolen our totems, I would be able to reward you myself. But...I shall have to do second best. Here is a history I have written that explains Palenqual's gift of living weapons to us.

Furthermore, I shall grant you permission to enter Palenqual's Caverns, where Kerehanua is waiting to help you create one of these weapons for yourself. Kerehanua's a chary old skinflint, so I wouldn't be surprised if he charged you a little bit for his weapons. Don't worry--his heart's in the right place. For now--seek out the visage of Tonkamu on the northern side of Wharu's Ridge, and you wi...

greetings: Hey, money! I appreciate it. Your contributions are welcome.
I heard a secret, but it'll cost you more than that.

So, Samuel in Eastham claims to have some sort of new wonder drink! He says it cured him of his nightmares. So, I went to the Singularity Caul, got some of those bits he makes the drink from, and gave them over... Can't say that it did much for me outside of clinging to my throat on the way down...
Have you found them yet? Those Singularity Caul reliquaries I keep hearing about? I hear people have found some strange items in them!
Lord Kresovus has put out a call for help. The Queen offered her aid, but he said he would rather seek assistance from independent adventurers. I wonder what that's all about?
The Queen is looking for help in finding out how Carlo di Cenza found his way to Dereth. Talk to Antius Blackmoor in Yaraq if you wish to help!
Last month I found what I thought was the most powerful sword I have yet come across. But this month, I found an even better one! This a good time to be a hunter!
Has that 50,000 pyreal piece of armor been cluttering up your house chest for too long? Well, go to Shoushi, Yaraq, or Holtburg and sell it!
A friend of mine was hunting the Singularity Caul when he came across a powerful new creature. It was a tough fight, he said, but he got a nifty spear out of the deal.

My good friend Loh-Gann Huhjj found a page from Carlo di Cenza's journal on the beach near the northern Beach Fort. It appears to be part of a much larger work. I sure hope he finds all the pieces. I am very interested in this Viamontian's past.
If you stand on the northern shores and listen closely enough, you can hear the screams of war. What madness makes its home up there? And when will it find its way to our lands?

Oh just like everyone else, my advice is only good enough for a paltry amount of pyreals! Well thank you, Mr. Pyrealbags this'll go a long way toward providing for my family. I'm sure that an egg will feed me, my three kids and my spouse.
Oh you just don't know...

Need a vassal? I won't ask for much just some tinkered armor and maybe a tinkered weapon. Oh and maybe a few MMD trade notes, or maybe some golem hearts, wasp wings, armoredillo spines, lugian sinews, dark revenant thigh bones, full sturdy iron key rings, full singularity key rings, or anything else that you don't need.
They say that Asheron went back home. I can't wait to see what he does, now that he's in control of the place.
Town criers are available in most major towns to tell you of the latest news and events. We'll also give you a piece of information for a bit of money.
Has it really been a year since poor Samuel was discharged from the Royal Guard? I would like to say Eastham was better for it, but... well... Sam hasn't done much outside of drink.
I can't wait to put this back together!
The Town Crier produces a handful of some blackened mineral.
Wait, you can't have this! It's mine! If you want some for yourself, you'll have to get it on your own!
I was speaking with a Lugian friend of mine the other day when he mentioned something about a great disturbance. He refused to elaborate, though I plied him with enough ale to drop a horse.
Have you read Carlo di Cenza's journal? I've never heard of a place called Shadow Pass, though I suspect the world outside of Dereth is much larger than we suspect.
If you're looking for some powerful weaponry, I recommend hunting some of Dereth's tougher creatures.
The vendors in Shoushi, Yaraq, and Holtburg must have benefited from those newly relocated casinos. They seem to have several more pyreals in their possession than usual.
What's the story behind these Banished creatures? They sure sound scary to me.
Who is this Sezzherei I keep hearing about? And what does he want with the Caul?
The Queen is greatly disturbed by the recent attack on the Royal Vaults. She fears we may not have heard the last of these mysterious Lugians.
The wind from the north grows cold. I fear a storm may be on the horizon.

Did you know that they moved us to a new pay schedule? We only get paid once a month, and only on the first day of the month. But I'm expected to be at my post the same amount of hours... Oh sure the town crier is here for you, but where's the love for us, huh?

So I'm sure you've noticed that I haven't left this spot in nearly four years. Yeah it's a tough life, standing here all day. Sure... sometimes people are nice enough to give me Shackles of Obedience. But I was wondering...Need a patron?

Aun Tanua gently cups the ember in his clawed hands, and as its glow warms his skin, his past gradually seeps into memory. For the first instant in an endless monotony of time, he remembers. Ezheret. Palenqual. Timaru. Home.
As determination and strength return to the old warrior's stance, he turns to you once more.

I have no knowledge of how long I have been imprisoned here. Endless half moments on moments, my memory failing, my own keh draining away...All I know is that I cannot leave, for the Atua ngamaru have me captured inside these walls of light.

My own Timaru is far from me, but you have brought me an ember of her heart, and once again my people are with me. You must have been sent with this gift by one of my brethren, and for that I thank you.
There is but one way to let my brothers envision my fate, and I must ask one more favor of you.

Aun Tanua lifts the akiekie ember to his face and softly blows across its faintly glowing surface. As his keh suffuses the ember, it suddenly fans into a flame. He holds it a moment longer, then relinquishes it to your care.
Give this to the one that sent you here to me. He will understand its intent and what should be done. Go now, and if you ever tread upon the shores of Palenqual, let her know I am with her.

Aun Tanua slowly turns towards you, surprise barely flickering across his careworn eyes.  He almost reaches out to touch your arm, but conditioned imprints of lightning-pain, years of throwing his fading body against electric walls, jolts a recoil through his frame.
A face. I see a face. Not Tonk. Not Atua ngamaru. I see a face.
Atual arutoa?
Aun Tanua starts shivering uncontrollably and shrinks within himself.
Not here. None here. Never here.
Tikakhe inspects the hide for any small imperfections and finds none.

This hide will do nicely to create a drumhead for your buadren. Use this Tanning Oil on it to make it into a suitable leather. Once you complete your drum, give it to me and I will enjoin Mighty Oak to infuse it with his keh.
Ah, you have found one of the limbs of Mighty Oak. If you hollow it out, it would make a perfect shell for a drum.
Shreth has given you one of his fiery hides. You must cut this into smaller straps to bind a Buadren together.
This hollow trunk is now ready to be a shell for a drum. Cover it with the Tanned Hide of an Ebon Mattekar, and it will nearly be complete.

All you need to do now is bind this drum together with Leather Straps cut from the hide of a Shreth Auroch. Once this task is complete, you will have created a Buadren. Bring this Buadren to me, and I will enjoin mighty Oak to enter it and sustain you with his keh.
This oil can be used to tan the hide of a Dread Mattekar into leather.

You have done a good job in tanning this hide. Now, if you drape it over a hollowed-out tree trunk, you will have completed most of the steps towards making a buadren for yourself. When you have completed one, give it to me, and I will enhance it for you.

These leather straps could be used to bind a tanned Dread Mattekar Hide to a drum shell made from a hollowed-out tree trunk. Together, this will form a buadren much like the ones we Tonk use to cast our spells.
No, friend, this buadren, created from the trophies of your own hunts and crafted through the work of your own hands, is rightfully yours.

This is an ember taken from the akiekie council fire of Timaru. The keh of our ancestors reside within that flame--if Aulakhe has entrusted you with an ember of that fire, he must have great faith in you.
This ember glows more brightly than ever before. Quickly, you must take it to Aulakhe before its life ebbs away.

It is as I have forseen. Aulakhe is the first among us to combine the medicine of our people and yours. The spirit of Aun Tanua has returned to fight the battles of his people once more. This buadren is infused with Tanua's own keh. If carried with reverence, he will aid you in your struggles as well.  Take our gift with pride, and  know that you have done the Tonk of Timaru a great service thi...

When Aulakhe first came and told me he was leaving Timaru, I knew I could not let him go alone. We have journeyed across the breadth of Dereth on our quest, and I have seen much that could be used to create semblances of the items we had back on Palenqual.
In the days since we have settled here, even more powerful spirits than before have pledged their aid in the creation of the Buadrens much like the one you see in my hands.
The great Aualuan Kenchaua has sent word from the mountains of the south that Ebon Mattekar pledged his hides to form Buadren's head.
Fire Shreth from the plains of the north has pledged his hides to form Buadren's sinews.
As we finally settled here, near the akiekie of Aula's new ani, Ispar Celdisethaua, Mighty Oak promised his limbs to form Buadren's body.

Once you assemble these three gifts, give the hide of Ebon Mattekar to me. I will inspect it for its imperfections--if it is perfect, I will give you a fragrant oil brought from Timaru to tan it into a supple drumskin. Tanae speed your hunt, friend.
quest: Tikakhe slowly turns the buadren over in his hands, inspecting every detail.
The spirits of this land are indeed generous. I could not have made a better buadren myself. Wait one moment, while I invoke the keh of Mighty Oak.

Beating gently upon the buadren, Tikakhe slowly murmurs a prayer to the anima of his choosing. A quiet descends upon the forest, and the trees themselves bend to listen to Tikakhe's call. Abruptly, a soft glow permeates the drum, one that is gone as suddenly as it came.

A last tale to tell before my work is done: I must tell you that this was merely a test, to prove to us that you are the warrior that we have journeyed from Palenqual to find. Aun Aulakhe's has undertaken a grave mission for our people, and we shall not return to our beloved Timaru until it is accomplished. Speak to him now--I will let him know that you have been chosen.
Aun Tikakhe pauses a moment to take you into his confidence.

Although he is still young and untested, my heart believes Aulakhe is destined one day to become the most gifted of our Aulauan, surpassing even his father, Shimauri. You would do well to guard this buadren safely--there may come a time when Aulakhe may be able to enhance it once more.
The spirits of this land are indeed generous. I could not have made a better buadren myself. Wait one moment, while I invoke the keh of Mighty Oak!

A last tale to tell before my work is done: my budhi Aun Aulakhe has undertaken a grave mission for our people, and we shall not return to our beloved Timaru until it is accomplished. Speak to him when you have gained in experience and strength - I will let him know that when that day comes he can take you into his confidence. Until then, guard this buadren safely--if you aid us in the days to...

greetings: %n stands protectively in front of his fledgling akiekie.
%n shivers and barely suppresses a sneeze.
Ah yes, here you are.

I stand here to protect my Aun brothers while they fullfill the mission entrusted to them by Shimauri. Our ancient rivalry with the Hea still stands, and I have seen untold numbers of their xuta during our tour of this land. It shall be as I have sworn: they shall not stray near our small akiekie while I am on guard.

Aulakhe has continued his studies with the great one,  Ispar Celdisethaua. He can now instill his Invokers with even more power. If he created one for you in the past, he has given me permission to exchange one of his newer ones for it.
Ah, the water, thank you.

You see that small sapling? It is very special to my people. You should be proud that we have chosen to plant it here. When it has grown it will represent the unity of our xuta's. I am asking the spirits to watch over her and give her the strength that we can share in our endeavors here.
Ah, yes.
She thanks you for the water. Once the grey-skins have done their work this tree and our akiekie will be fed from the water which lies below.
Oh, a visitor! Fetch me some water for this tree and I will tell you of my labors.
Hello no-tail! Do you like our tree? She will stand taller than most and stronger than some. Bring me water so that I may continue my drumming.
I'm sorry, I can't talk at the moment. This spell must be cast with precise drumming. Bring me some water. I should be done with the difficult magics by then and will talk with you.
Did you see her keh swell? It's so beautiful! She is growing faster than I could have hoped. All this work makes it thirsty though.
You have done well to bring this to us, friend, but I fear I am not the proper person to receive it from you. Take this to Aun Ngationa there; he can receive it from you.
Greetings! I am Aun Turiona, and I am here in Timaru to learn statecraft from my kinsman Aun Hareltah. If I learn well, I may one day act as envoy to your people.
Aun Hareltah has tasked me with rewarding any no-tail who defeats Hea Temepuh. Give me the Totem of Temepuh and I will give you the Kalindan of Palenqual.

The Totem of Temepuh! Aun Hareltah will want to see this at once! But ...
Aun Turiona looks puzzled. She cups the totem in the palm of her hand and closes her eyes. She shakes her head, studies the totem closely, and then frowns at you.
You attempt to deceive me. You did not kill the scourge of the uplands.

greetings: The Totem of Temepuh! You have done well to bring this to us, friend, but I fear I am not the proper person to receive it from you. You should speak with my kinsmen Kiriona, Rukuona, and Turiona.
This is a wondrous item! My thanks to you for allowing me to work with it! Here, I will just tighten this, and loosen ... hmmm ... That's not right.
Aun Ngationa frowns at the buadren, turning it over and over in his hands.
Well ... here you are! Do you like my work? If you are not pleased, I can put it back the way it was ... I think.
Well, I am still learning after all. Let me repair this for you.
Truly a spear of legend! Let me try to modify it for you. I think that this will work... Here you are!
If you don't like the results, I can change it back for you.
Truly a vicious scalpel! Let me try to modify it for you. I think that this will work... Here you are!
What an amazing bow! Let me try to modify it for you. I think that this will work... Here you are!
Let me try to modify this crop for you. I think that this will work... Here you are!

Aun Hareltah has asked me to assist our drummers by organizing any bits of stone debris or rubble that can be found. I will sort this debris, and send it out to our drummers where it can do the most good. If you bring me a piece of rubble I will reward you well for it -- although if you wish to aid us more directly, you should still take the rubble directly to the proper menhir ring.
In addition, I have also been experimenting with modifying certain buadrens. If you happen to possess the Awakener of Hea Karenua, I will modify it for you.

greetings: No thanks, I think the shamman could use some water though.
I knew you were good for something!  You just don't find enough writing paper on beasts anymore.  Don't you wish that all creatures carried more parchment?
Thanks! It's really dry out here and I keep getting too involved in my work to remember to drink something.
Oh, for me?
Mrmrmmm, good...
Ah! That was good. I feel much better now. Your not such a bad no-tail, not like that last one I met. Make sure that you help us build the town by donating materials.
quest: You destroyed my day's work! Now I have to go back and recalculate all of the distances! Get out of my sight, you bahka!
I know you are eager to help, but please do not fool with my tripod.
You would be interrupting my important work for something very important, yes?
No? Then please go bother someone else!
Did you come all the way out here just to make my job even harder?
I swear I placed my last piece of parchment right here.
I must record the latest measurements before the next bahka comes along and decides it's funny to destroy my work.
Oh no, I don't mean you, I'm sure you are a very nice no-tail and looks aren't everything.
I'm sorry, it's been a rough day.  We're on a tight schedule and sometimes I lose my temper.  Surveying is a thankless job, you know.

greetings: Do not disturb my watch. The town depends on me to stay ever vigilant.
Yes, I can see your house from here, now leave me to my watch.
Go bug the gate guard or something. Can't you see I'm trying to defend the town from hordes of creatures bent upon our destruction?

There have been reports of odd portal disruptions in this area. I've been sent to this outpost to keep watch. If you're new to this land, for safety's sake I'd suggest you stay well within the Arcanum's perimeter of Obelisks--at least until you're strong enough to venture out on your own.
Our Sparring Golems seem to be hemorrhaging tokens these days. Thanks--I'll return it to the Practice Area for you.
No thanks, I have no need for your Welcome Letter. Save it for later--someone in Holtburg may have a use for them.
No, thank you. This is for you to read and remember.
A fine piece. I remember the day I created my first Academy weapon well. This is yours, to remember us by.
No thanks, I have no need for your Welcome Letter. Save it for later--someone in Shoushi may have a use for them.
No thanks, I have no need for your Welcome Letter. Save it for later--someone in Yaraq may have a use for them.
The %n scans the area for any encroaching dangers.
We are here to guard the people of this town against any future attacks. If you have any questions, you should talk to the Senior Guard assigned to lead our garrison.
Thank you! You have done the Dereth Exploration Society a great service. Take this last gift from us at the Academy; it will serve you well in your initial travels.

Now, you must leave this place. There is nothing more that we can teach you here. Use the portal to Shoushi. When you get there, seek out Oi-Tong Ye. He may have a task for you. Take care in your adventures, friend.
You must be the one the Senior Guard told me about. Thank you for your assistance.
A hive of Olthoi just breached the Outer Wall. They stole a collection of Protection Orbs. Without those orbs, we have no way of shielding ourselves from their Queen!
You must infiltrate the hive and travel as deep into it as you can. Find the Adolescent Olthoi and kill it. Bring back one of those orbs!
Go!

Now, you must leave this place. There is nothing more that we can teach you here. Use the portal to Yaraq. When you get there, seek out Mara al-Luq. She may have a task for you. Take care in your adventures, friend.

She is the Explorer Society Agent in Holtburg; you can recognize her by her green robes. You will find her in the bar, which will be ahead of you and very slightly to the right when you exit the portal.
No, thank you. You should keep this for your records. Now you should use the portal to Holtburg to continue your adventures in Dereth.
The Sentry senses your arrival and slowly struggles to her feet.

You have arrived, at last. A devastating force of Hollow Minions just swept through the Outer Courtyard...who sent them, I know not. Whoever it was empowered them with an unspeakable strength...and I've now just received word that twelve of the Arrival Points have been completely destroyed. We can only be thankful that our Queen had the foresight to fortify this one. Please patrol the Outer Cou...
What's this?
As the Sentry struggles to read the tattered parchment in the failing light, a wild comprehension crossed with fear dawns across her face. She begins to mutter softly to herself.

Martine's minions. We should have known... With his disappearance it was only a matter of time before his minions struck out on their own. We must endeavour to redouble our efforts against this new...
The Sentry suddenly becomes aware of your presence once more and pulls herself together.
You have helped us more than you can know. Take this last gift from us at the Academy--it will serve you well in your initial travels.
Also, you should keep this. Save it for your records of these strange occurrances.

Defending the town my Patron!
I'm on patrol serving the greater good.

My brothers have stationed themselves across this land, hunting the strongest of the creatures you call golems. They are not selfish, and during the times that they are at rest, they will be happy to share in the hunt and reward those who have taken up the same challenge as they. Please go visit them.
Greetings. I am Aun Kielerea, a hunter for the Aun Xuta. My brothers and I have ventured away from the land of Palenqual to seek out mightier prey than what can be found near our home.
This does not mean we have forsaken Aun Hareltah, rather that we are looking for glorious battle against truly worthy opponents. And we believe we have found it!
May you always be brave in battle.
You have told me a tale of victory too recently. Come back after a few moons with a new tale of victory and I will share in my bounty.

Greetings. I am Aun Tahuirea. My seven sons have left the land of Palenqual in search of glorious hunts. No doubt trying to impress me. They are each talented hunters in their own right, but none of them are yet ready to hunt what I do.

What is it that I hunt, you ask? I keep my harpoon sharp for the rare Crystal Lords. They are a dangerous type of golem for ones such as you, so be sure to bring others of your xuta to aid you in the battle. Should you and your fellows come across and defeat one, please come speak with me. I would enjoy hearing the story of your battles.
Also, if you and your fellows succeed in defeating one, I will be pleased to share with you the bounties I have recovered from my previous victories.

You tell Tahuirea the tale of the battle you and your fellows waged against the Crystal Lord and its minions. The Elder Tumerok smiles throughout the entire story. As you finish, Tahuirea unclips a key from his belt and hands it to you.

Your tale was truly one of triumph! I only wish I could have been there to see the battle for the tale is one of incredible glory. Use this key to take some of the bounty I have amassed in my hunting of the Crystal Lords.

greetings: This looks to be a very important report. I think that this should be delivered to Captain K'rank. I do not wish to keep such an important report from his hands.
I have been sent by High Queen Elysa to reward those who have assisted Captain K'rank of Linvak Tukal. If you have proof of this assistance give it to me and I will see that you are rewarded.
quest: Aun Faranua says, "Hail %tn. I see that you have returned to shatter the morale of the Burun again. Your efforts continue to assist our people in lessening the threat these creatures pose. Here are your rewards."
The key will open whichever chest you choose in that room. Each chest should clearly display what it holds.
Aun Faranua says, "That is all that I have to give. Thank you again for your efforts, %tn."

Aun Faranua says, "Hail %tn. Again you take the head of the Burun leader, Morgluuk. You are surely a hero to all. As we have already placed the creatures head outside of the city in your honor, this one will be turned into a trophy that you can display with honor, %tn."
%tn has defeated Morgluuk and received a glorious reward for their efforts.
You should also be able to draw your rewards from the High Queen's treasure as well. Here take this key and this gem.
As you know, this key opens whichever chest you choose within that room. You are due just another small token, %tn.
Aun Faranua says, "That is all I have to give. You are a hero to us all, %tn."
Filthy creatures these Burun. As promised you are to be rewarded for your efforts.
A brave warrior who has continued our efforts to crush the morale of the Burun and the renegades. You have done well. Here take this and display it proudly.
The High Queen also wishes you to take a small reward from her coffers. Take these.
The key will open whichever chest you choose within the treasure room to which the gem brings you.
Aun Faranua exclaims, "%tn, you have killed the Burun leader, Morgluuk! This head is proof of what you have done. All should know your name."

%tn has slain Morgluuk and returned his head to the Tonk capital of Timaru. There it is to be placed on a pike as a symbol of victory for the Isparian, Lugian and Tumerok people and a symbol of defeat for the Burun that threaten our way of life. Huzzah, %tn!
You must be rewarded for your efforts.

Aun Faranua says, "The portal gem will take you into the High Queen's Vault. There you will find many chests that house treasures and weaponry that has been worked on by the finest smiths in the land. Take your gift and use it well, %tn. You are deserved of much praise in this victory."
Aun Faranua says, "That is the final reward I have for you. You have become a hero to all of Dereth, %tn. I shall never forget your name or your deeds."

greetings: I'm hungry.
As %s smashes Morgluuk, the Guruk in the area grow more agitated and the Ruuk become more docile!
As the Titan dies, it let's out a wail. Morgluuk will send his personal guard of Guruk to investigate. Morgluuk's lair will be weaker.
Mgrauleshk lets out a wail and collapses in a heap, slain by %s.
With a mighty croak, Mgrauleshk, snaps his head back in anger. A deadly spray of acid squirts from his hide.
As you open a large gash along Mgrauleshk's hide you are struck with a wave of noxious fumes. The wound begins to knit immediately.
Your blow tears a patch of flesh from Mgrauleshk's hide. As it falls away, a sour smell assails your nostrils and acid shoots from his hide.
With a chortle, Mgrauleshk reels his head back and retaliates for your assault.
Your blow bites deeply into Mgrauleshk's body. The giant reels a bit under the blow and then seems to be washed in a glow of mana.
You wound the giant deeply. The scent of a heady fungus flows about the area and Mgrauleshk's hide looks to have become thicker.
Mgrauleshk curls his lips toward you as you open a wound on his flesh. A spray of acid leaps from the wound.
As you open a wound on Mgrauleshk's hide, you are overwhelmed with a feeling of nausea.
You wound Mgrauleshk grievously. But the wound also allows a fetid scent to escape the beast.
Your tear into Mgrauleshk's hide, wounding the beast and sending a foul cloud of spores into the air.
As the magic from your spell dissipates around Mgrauleshk, you are struck with a wave of darkness that drains all strength and understanding from your body.
What can only be described as laughter, escapes Mgrauleshk's mouth. His retaliation is swift and potent.

Finding your attempt to bestow ill magics upon him laughable, Broodu responds with a spell of his own.
A deep gurgle that sounds like a laugh issues from Broodu. The air around him becomes foul.
Your magic dissolves around the buulky King. He finds your impotence amusing and responds with a vile enchantment.
A look of amusement courses through Broodu's eyes and he croaks out an incantation that falls upon you.
As your magic fails to penetrate Broodu's defenses he absently waves a hand weakening your connection to mana.
As your spell trickles harmlessly away into nothingness, Broodu finds amusement in causing you more grief.
Finding a trickle of mana drift away from your failed attack, Broodu turns the errant mana into a formidable assault.
A glimmer of recognition lights in Broodu's Eye. Your feeble attempt at casting a spell upon him has earned you his attention.
Laughing, Broodu retaliates for your failed assault.
Your magic dissipates, but you have earned the notice of the Burun King.

greetings: You feel something without voice scream in your mind in utter rage. It chills you to the bone as it fades away.
The black sarcophagus pulses with a black light.
As the Doll dies, it screams, "Doll has displeased Masters!  Invasion recedes, Masters will be angry..."  The forces gathered to assault Cragstone are pushed back...
As the Doll dies, it screams, "Doll has displeased Masters!  Invasion recedes, Masters will be angry..."  The forces gathered to assault Hebian-To are pushed back...
As the Doll dies, it screams, "Doll has displeased Masters!  Invasion recedes, Masters will be angry..."  The forces gathered to assault Zaikhal are pushed back...
Your vision swims. A wall of arid heat slams into your face, nearly  knocking you back. You blink, eyes dry and stinging.

You stand over a raw lava flow. The craggy walls are black stone, scarcely lit by the damask shadows from the liquid earth that rolls and flops beneath you. Down in the flow, figures are moving; constellations of stone, burning white from their inhospitable wading pool.

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be sitting before an orb wreathed in sourceless, clean blue flame. Across from you sits a young man, his hands  knotted in anguish, his golden eyes flaring with anger. He speaks, the words flowing like the musical speech of the sea peoples of Ispar. Like an afterimage, the words come again a moment later, in your own tongue. "Someone has to do someth...
You hear words, as if from your own mouth, saying, "But what can you do?"
"I can do what's right. I'm going back with the next study group," he says, looking at you carefully. "Maybe... for good."
"How could you stay without being found as something... other?"

The man laughs, a bitter thing. "The same way we take our smug notes. We don't hide away in hunting blinds, you know. The life masters create flesh glamors for us. I've strolled through the markets, smelling the crops." He rubs his head, chin ducking with some faint embarrassment. "Being that short takes some getting used to."

Your vision swims. For a moment, you stand upon a crest, a frigid wind blowing icy knives through you, the land dropping away from your toes. You stumble back a step back from the precipice, dazzled by the light that skitters and skips across the snowy ground. Squinting, you raise a hand against the light of the dying sun to see...

Mount Esper. But not as you know it. Heat haze causes the sun to dance a jig as the cinder cone's lake boils white. On all sides, people and golems move about. A floating stone pallet is loaded with bars of greenish gold metal; a white-hot golem illuminates the entry shaft it trundles out of, the the echo filling the crater with the sound of a mountain falling down.

You turn to your left. An distinguished elderly woman looks to the west, the clean white light of the sun sharpening the crags of her cheeks. One hand rests on a platinum cane inscribed with fine, elegant calligraphy. Impossibly, you know her friend Ejan made it for her. And impossibly, you find yourself speaking words you cannot guess the meanings of; and you seem to hear it in Roulean. "Shaur...

"Time will come when these things will be again," the old woman smiles, her silver hair glinting in the waning sun. "Don't worry, my dear. When all has fallen down, you and I will be there to rebuild it, won't we?"

Her storm-grey eyes turn away to the west again, like ship sailing over sea. Distantly, she murmurs, "He's a good boy, Resanne. I believe in him. Unlike that daft Emperor who has us make him coins as the olthoi approach."

Your vision swims. For a moment, you see a group of men and women in white and purple. Somehow, you recognize the pattern of the robes; the colors of the Knorr Lyceum. The fabric is torn, sweat-stained, the anonymous faces floating above them white with fatigue. You are jostled and shoved into a group. You blink into the shadows. What..? The adepts raise their hands. Their eyes fill with radian...
You fall into the silvered tube of portalspace. It snakes and writhes, following safe courses through dimensions no eye can see, and magic can scarcely chart. And then...
The tunnel does not collapse as it always does. It peels open. You are weightless, formless, tumbling through an empty violet abyss. So tired... Sleep...
And something, somewhere, tears a little more...
Your vision swims.
Violet light.
Crackflash.
A column of blue light, vague as smoke, shimmers briefly in the distance.
Am I awake? He said we would --
There's something moving in the light...

The vision releases you abruptly, leaving you trembling and breathless.

Your vision swims. For a moment, your vision dims. Great wooden doors, intricately carved and glowing faintly green, creak open before you. Before you is a long, wide hall, its cloistered ceilings lit by false stars that mime the constellations of the sky outside. Niches along both sides are lined with candles. No... not candles, but simple silver rods, tarnish blackening the hollows of their f...

Musical, incomprehensible speech calls your attention to the end of the great hall. A figure stands there, backlit by a roiling white inferno as blinding as the sun. A long shadow, unleavened by the waterlight from the silver rods, paints the marble at your feet. Like an echo, the meaning of the words comes back at you.

"Raen Ameranten. Chevaird of the Ialarchess. Child of Atermore, the  Alabaster Fortress that Rises from the sea; the Rock which guards the eastern ways of the glorious Imperial Archipelago. You are here required to swear the Rule of Life. Will you walk upon the path of a righteous life, in fear of and in service to the clear Light? Or will you turn aside to darkness, as have others of your orde...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to stand in creaking jungle. You are running, swinging a sword wreathed in astral flames. A hundred men around you roar as one. There! At last, the ornate blue spires rise before you. Ridiculous lizard-men flap towards you, their eyes glowing. Women dressed in the skins of animals raise their hands, and the ground erupts. You swim forward, wading throug...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem be running down stairs. Men lining the walls grin at you, bowing as you pass. They smell of sweat and blood, their white, star-branded campaign cloaks stained a lurid incarnadine. Their nostrils are flaring. Lips pull back from grey and brown teeth. You hold the torch above your head.

The women huddle together in the center of the blue stone room, watching the men with cool, detached defiance. Is that how it is? We'll see how long that detachment lasts. You nod to the men. One steps forward and wrenches a heretic girl out of the group, bending her arm a way it is not meant to go, driving her down to bruise her knees on the stones of the floor. She does not scream. The beads...
The room is silent but for the snapping of your torch. A lone bird cries in jungle outside.

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be staggering up a flight of stairs. A fetor rises from the room below, the stink of the slaughterhouse. They never made a sound. None of them, not even once, not even when the blades began to hew. Men follow you up, slapping each other on the back, laughing too much as they adjust their campaign cloaks. The air is no cleaner above, though. Here the...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be on the deck of a ship. A ship? There are no... Over the rail you can see docks carved from alabaster and chalcedony. Where? A crowd that roars. Shrill. The clouds recoil over the glittering spires of the city, and black rain descends on buzzing alien wings. The deck lurches - you find yourself clutching the wall of the dungeon.

What, it isn't flashy enough for you? Too bad!
That's as good as it gets! Now let me return to my work!
Could you have found anything heavier to give me?
Smelt that first. Sure I could smelt that Iron for you, but then what would you do with your ample free time?
I seem to remember giving this to you for you to use.
examines the book closely.
Hah, got it back from that drunkard, did you? Only a fool lets himself lose as much as he has.  Once, he was the greatest of his generation.  Did you know that?
You'd never think it to see the sot he is now - well, you got my book back, so you deserve that reward.
By the way, I'd be careful when you use that spell.
%n snickers.
Now leave me in peace.
Found the iron eh? Well, give me a minute.
%n's eyes glow briefly for a moment
There it's fixed, now don't let the door hit you on the way out. And don't come back!
Never seen an Empyrean before? Shoo! Shoo! I have work to do.
Did you know that Empyreans have 14 schools of magic? Would you like me to demonstrate them all on you?
It was so much better when you people thought I was one of you. That's impossible now though, thanks to that cretin Gaerlan.
What, looking for some great quest, some grand purpose from the Empyrean? Go away!
I liberate some of your people from a despotic ruler...think you could show a little bit of respect!
Alfrega, Alfrega girl! Fresh meat!
Off with you, I'm a busy mage!
Go away! And don't tell Asheron I'm down here! Never could stand the man...
You best not have done anything to Alfrega, if you know what's good for you...
Well if you are going to continue to bother me, you can at least do something for me. Take this note to Celcynd in Rithwic.
He borrowed one of my history books sometime ago and didn't return it because he became a drunken waste. Probably spilled alcohol all over it.
Go get it and I'll give you some scroll I've got lying around here...or not. Will you leave me alone then?
I don't want this back.
You'd never think it to see the sot he is now - and all because of this cursed spell, which he lacked the strength to cast twice, when it was needed most.
Regardless, a deal is a deal, and it's your problem if it fails you.  Now go away, and don't bother me anymore!
What would I want with this?  Have you been drinking this?  I know what you young fools do with such things!  Begone, before I report you to the Knights of the Golden Flame!
Fine. Take the staff, don't let the door hit you on the way out. And don't come back!
What? I ALREADY fixed this. Go away before I call Alfrega in here!
You couldn't find something heavier to give me, eh? I'll tell you secret...I have no interest in your lump of iron ore!
If you gave me a good reason, I might help you smelt the ore, but right now I have to tie my shoes.
Listen, if I wanted a pot I would have asked you for one!
Who are you?
Who sent you?
What do you want?
Leave me alone!
Go away!
Bah. I have no time for this!
Stop wasting my time! I'm a busy mage!
You'd best not have harmed my pet Reedshark, Alfrega!
Alfrega! Here girl! There's a tasty snack bothering me!

Well, if you're here, why don't you make yourself useful. Celcynd, the planar mage from Rithwic, borrowed one of my histories a few years back, and never returned it because he became a drunken waste.
Get it for me, and I'll give you a portal spell scroll he gave me. Will you leave me alone then?

That should be enough to fix this piece of cr...

...er, treasured relic and give me some peace and quiet. Now, off with you.
I'm not going to fix another of these for you! Go away before I call Alfrega on you
