You will get nothing from me for this. Go explore and find more towns.  The Society Agents in the Sho towns will exchange a piece of jewelry or a wand for this. If you take this to one of the Aluvian towns, you will receive a piece of armor.

greetings: Thanks. I have to have something in case you run off with my key.  I'll have you know it was fashioned by the best lockpi... finest craftsman in Uziz!
Straight southeast from here, you'll find an old dry well.  Go down into it, and bring me back some well water.  And don't you believe those stories about the lower caves being haunted!
Hah! My thanks, gentle friend. Here's that 200p I promised you.
Some people believe that since this water comes from an old Empyrean well, it's enchanted. As the Poet said, we're short of everything but foolishness, eh? But if they'll pay, I'll sell.
What's this? This isn't water from the well - it's too clean! You're trying to swindle me, Malik take your eyes! I'll not give you a single Pyreal for this!
Say, I might have 200 nice, shiny Pyreals with your name on them!  I'll have you know this key was fashioned by the best lockpi... finest craftsman in Uziz!
Straight southwest from here, you'll find an old dry well.  Go down into it, and bring me back some well water.  And don't you believe those stories about the lower caves being haunted!
Thank you.  I believe you can succeed.

The Unfinished Temple is to the northwest of here.  We fled pretty far into the ruins before we realized we had to leave.  I think we were at least two levels down when we lost the knives.  Last I was there, I found only one knife.
That is definitely one of my mother's knives!  Thank you.
Here is a letter to take to my sister Jilsaya in Al-Arqas.  She has a task for you.
Long ago, on the way to Al-Arqas, my mother and I came upon a ruin and camped there.  At night, monsters came upon us, and after holding them off for a while, we fled.
We left behind my mother's collection of knives, among the first she ever forged.  They are not worth very much, but I will help you if you get one for me.
Yes, you would be great for this task.  To the west of here is a crypt in which drudges have taken up residence.
Some drudges are known to carry charms, and I know there is usually one lying around in that crypt.  Please get it to me, and I shall help you out.
Hello.  I have a task that I am just too tired to do myself.  There is a crypt near here from which I would like an item.
quest: Thank you.  I turn these in to Collectors for a monetary reward.  But I will give you something better.
Here is a letter to take to Jilsaya bint Dah in Al-Arqas.
Thank you, but I have enough for now.  Why don't you check again tomorrow?

greetings: Your arrival at this time could only be providence.
Could you rush this to Nasun in the North Yaraq Outpost? He is a bit smitten with Mara, and would wish to sign it.
Ha!  Only for fair Mara would Nasun write sooner than I.  And overwritten, as usual.  He does love his vocabulary.
Since you are here, would you do us the honor of presenting this note to Mara, at her father's villa outside Yaraq?  I am sure she will be pleased to receive it.

My friend Mara al-Luq in Yaraq has just received some happy news, and I want to congratulate her.  Could you rush this to Nasun in the North Yaraq Outpost? He is a bit smitten with Mara, and would wish to sign it first.
quest: My apologies for the length of the errand.  I did not think that both Nasun and Mara would ask you to carry mail as well.
Take this, then, and my blessings on your journey.
But you just gave me her letter!  Maybe if you come back tomorrow with a new letter, I will believe that it is her.

greetings: I remember a man, or maybe it was a woman, I am not truly sure so many people come through here to talk to me. At any rate they bought a large quantity of my Cove Apple Cider not long ago.
Wait, wait... I think it was Ulgrim the Unpleasant.
It's certainly not bark from on of the trees in my cove. Maybe it's from up north.
I'm sorry, this looks like it belongs to someone else. You might try Ulgrim.
I don't deal in fineries of this type. But I know that tailors do. In fact this looks like To-ping Ra's work.
The sea is beautiful, is it not? I should miss it if we find a way to return to our deserts in Ispar.
Oh, those cursed Drudges... Can't they find someplace else to steal food from?
Another shipment of cider waylaid by Drudges... may their bones be devoured by sand!
I know not where you found this, but it is not from my orchard. My Cove Apples are the finest in Dereth.
This isn't my daughter's! I can tell just by smelling it.
You know, I used to have faith in my fellow man, but trying to pass this bruised apple for one found in my orchard re-affirms my belief that people are untrustworthy!
Ah, yes. You must have found this in the orchard. Allow me to gift you with one of my daughter's pies.
One of my good apples! Thank you so much!
My special baking pan! You know, I made this myself - it helps keep the juicy goodness in the pie. Thank you so much!
My special apple knife! You know, I made this myself. It's especially sharp, so that I don't bruise the apples as I cut them. Thank you so much!
Ah, some of the good stuff! You have my thanks!
Ah, some of the very good stuff! You have my thanks!
Ah, some of the best stuff! You have my thanks!
Thank you for returning this pie! It's even still hot - that was quick work!
My daughter baked one of her pies for you! She makes the finest in the A'mun Desert. Not that there's much competition out here, mind. But don't tell her I said that!
You know, since you've been so helpful to me, perhaps you could also help my friend Ma'yad ibn Ibsar. Her brother is missing, and she is very worried.
You can find Ma'yad in the bar in Yaraq proper.
What is this?
Lubziklan al-Luq reads the letter.
Bah! I've no time for this right now.
Those pesky Drudges have broken into my wine cellar and are drinking all my wine.
Perhaps if you were to solve my problem, I'd consider signing a trade agreement with Anton

The Drudges have taken over my wine cellar. In fact, no one even remembers it as Lubziklan's cellar anymore. Those Drudges have turned it into a right hovel, I tell you! You can find it just southeast of here.
Bring back my Cove Apple Wine and we'll talk.
This is the most spectacular apple I have ever seen!
I must have it! Perhaps I can grow a tree from this.
I don't drink this myself, but it's popular with the mages. Thank you for returning it to me.
Can I help you, traveler? Well, but perhaps you can help me.

I am the owner of the orchards, and the purveyor of delicious and sundry goods made from the finest Cove apples. Lately, though, I am beleaguered by a pesky band of drudges that has been stealing all my goods! I need someone who is willing to defeat these drudges and recover my goods for me.
Here is a list of what they have taken. Return these items to me and I will reward you appropriately.

I believe that these drudges are holed up in the Sea Temple Catacombs, on a plateau at the mouth of the harbor. But rumor has it that there is an easier entrance, through the Rat's Nest just northwest of town.
If you need more help finding either location, you can buy directions from Jubal at the bar in Yaraq proper.
quest: You were only able to retrieve one bottle!
It was my best batch of wine too.
Well, you certainly tried your best.
And I'm sure those Drudges will think twice before they steal from me again.
I did some thinking while you were away and decided that this Anton Silezzi might be on to something.
So I have decided to join his network of merchants.
Take this letter to him.
That's for you to keep. Enjoy!
You found something of Abmim's! Quick, take this to Ma'yad in Yaraq! She must be worried sick!
I don't want this! But it looks like the sort of thing Akyafi might be interested in. Why don't you try taking it to him?
My dear daughter Mara is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to her? She can usually be found in the bar in town.

greetings: What a kind gesture of Ahyara's! Thank you for bringing this to me! But didn't she ask you to take this to Nasun first?
Oh, how sweet of Nasun! Thank you for bringing this to me! But didn't he as you to take this to Ahyara first?
How kind of Ahyara to think of me! Could you carry this thank-you note back to her for me?
Oh, what a sweet man Nasun is! I wish I could understand but half of his words, but I know he means well.
Please, would you take him this thank-you note?
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Hey, looks like it got rolled in the mud... Anyway, well done!  Here, take these as a reward.
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Looks like good old F.P. went swimming or something.  Here's your reward.
Looks like you've lucked out!  Our man F.P. has finished his book, finally!  Here you go...
You'd rather cast this spell on your own?
Well I can't argue with that.
Greetings! Welcome to Yaraq! I am the local representative of the Explorer Society. My job is to help new arrivals in Dereth get settled in and learn their way around.
If you have just arrived in Dereth, my father Lubziklan could really use your help. And if you can help him, he can help you get a good start on your new life here in Dereth.
Seek him out at our house just to the south of town, near the beach. If you need help finding it, you can buy directions from Jubal, the barkeeper.
It has also been requested that I start handing out these gems.
quest: Yes, I baked that for you. Enjoy!
My father Lubziklan is looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
You found something of Abmim's! Quick, take this to Ma'yad! She must be worried sick!
I believe that Akyafi the Translator was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
Ahha! Thank you for bringing this to me!

I have been contracted by the Dereth Exploration Society to help them in their outreach program towards the Isparians who find themselves newly exiled in Dereth.  Here is a book that explains their mission.
I will also give you a list describing the locations of the nearest stamp and portals to other towns.  If you collect any of the Society's stamped letters, you may bring them back to me for a reward.
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here.  You are a true Explorer!

You will get nothing from me for this. Go explore and find more towns.  The Society Agents in the Sho towns will exchange a piece of jewelry or a wand for this. If you take this to one of the Aluvian towns, you will receive a piece of armor.

greetings: Many thanks, friend traveler.
Would you have the time to bring this to Ahyara in the East Yaraq Outpost? She is also a friend of Mara's, and would wish to sign this small note as well.
As ever, Ahyara is swifter to act than I.  Ah well.
My friend, could I trouble you to bring this to Mara at her father's villa outside Yaraq? I am sure she will be pleased to receive it.
My friend Mara al-Luq, the flower of Yaraq, has just received some happy news, and I want to congratulate her.
quest: Ah, Mara's spirit is as lovely as her face!  You have my thanks, friend traveler,  for performing this little errand. I pray it was not too onerous.
Please accept this small token of my appreciation.
But you just gave me her letter!  Maybe if you come back tomorrow, I will believe that she has written me again.

greetings: The Stone of Discipline! This stone represents the discipline that a follower of Jojii must maintain - discipline over their fears and their desires.
Thank you for bringing this to me.
The Stone of Detachment! This stone represents the detanchment that a follower of Jojii must maintain - detachment from the illusions and pitfalls of the material realm.
The Stone of Compassion! A follower of Jojii must temper their detachment with compassion. Compassion cuts through the illusion of the material realm as a ray of light through the gloom.

The Stone of Humility! A follower of Jojii must temper their discipline with humility. When you discipline your fears and desires, you bring yourself closer to the central principle of life - but no mere human can maintain that closeness indefinitely. You will make mistakes. When you no longer make mistakes, you will no longer be human.
If you are looking for more adventure, friend, then you might want to speak with the lovely Nin Hong upstairs. She maintains a library of gossip and rumors that may serve you well in this.
Take this -- but if you would prefer an atlatl, I have those too. Just hand the bow back to me.
Take this -- but if you would prefer at atlatl, I have those too. Just hand the bow back to me.
Ah, a truly adventurous soul. Here you are!
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Hey, looks like it got rolled in the mud... Anyway, well done!  Here, take these as a reward.
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Looks like good old F.P. went swimming or something.  Here's your reward.
Looks like you've lucked out!  Our man F.P. has finished his book, finally!  Here you go...
You'd rather cast this spell on your own?
Well I can't argue with that.
Greetings, and welcome to Shoushi. I am the local representative of the Explorer Society. My job is to help new arrivals in Dereth.
If you have just arrived in Dereth, you should talk to my friend Lou Ka, who stands just over there. He is looking for some help with an errand.
Or you might investigate the rumors that the lovely Nin Hong sells upstairs.
It has also been requested that I start handing out these gems.
quest: I believe that Lou Ka was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
I believe that Nen Ai was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to her?
Ahha! Thank you for bringing this to me!

I have been contracted by the Dereth Exploration Society to help them in their outreach program towards the Isparians who find themselves newly exiled in Dereth.  Here is a book that explains their mission.
I will also give you a list describing the locations of the nearest stamp and portals to other towns.  If you collect any of the Society's stamped letters, you may bring them back to me for a reward.
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here.  You are a true Explorer!

You will get nothing from me for this. Go explore and find more towns.  The Society Agents in the Gharun'dim towns will exchange a piece of jewelry or a wand for this. If you take this to one of the Aluvian towns, you will receive a weapon.

greetings: You have recovered my yaoji! Thank you so much!
I never thought I'd see this again! You have my thanks!
The mosswarts love to throw these for some reason. Thank you for bringing this one back to me!
Ah, my favorite katar. Thank you.
Bai Den will be thrilled to have this back! Thank you!
This is Bai Den's favorite bracelet. Those mosswarts keep stealing it - perhaps because it glitters so.
Bai Den was given this ring by his mother. It has great sentimental value to him. Thank you so much for bringing it back to us!
You have our sincere thanks for returning this to us.

Since you've been so kind as to help us, perhaps you could also help our friend Nen Ai. She lives just outside Shoushi, a bit further down the southwest road than the Braid Mansion Ruin you were just at.
Nen Ai has a pet drudge. She has some trouble keeping it fed, however - it has a delicate constitution. Perhaps you could visit her and see if you could help?
Here are the directions to Nen Ai's house. Nin Hong also sells these directions.
Those thieving mosswarts have made off with my yaoji again! And this time they took several other items belonging to myself and my partner Bai Den as well!
Here is a list of the items that are missing. Will you go to the Braid Mansion Ruin, along the road that leaves town to the southwest, and recover our things for us? We would be very grateful.
If you need more help finding the Braid Mansion Ruin, you can buy directions from Nin Hong at the bar.
quest: I believe that Nen Ai, in her house along the southwest road,  was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to her?
That's some stone you have there. Oi-Tong Ye collects these, I believe - why don't you show it to him?
Oi-Tong Ye is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to him?

greetings: You have found the cider! My little friend will be so excited! It makes him the least bit tipsy, you know.
Allow me to reward you.
This cheese is very strengthening. I am most grateful that you have brought it to me so that I may feed it to my beloved pet.
You have been so good to help me already, but perhaps you can do one more thing for me?

My friend Oi-Tong Ye follows the teachings of Jojii. He has been searching for four stones that represent the Jojiist principles of Discipline, Detachment, Compassion, and Humility. I have recently learned that these stones may be found in the Shreth Hive.

Here are directions that will lead you to the Shreth Hive. Please see if you can recover the four stones. When you do, take them to Oi-Tong Ye in the bar in Shoushi. He will be so pleased to have them!
%n carefully takes and reads the scroll.
Oh my, more food for the little Drudges? I hope she is giving them to good homes.
%n pens a response for Larinne Kerendova.
Here, give her this letter and tell her I'll happily make up another batch of food for her little Drudges.
I have tended this drudge since it was very young, and he is my friend. But he is still very weak.
There are two foods that he particularly likes and which help him grow strong. These are perfectly aged Greenmire Cider, and perfectly aged Greenmire Cheese.
Would you retrieve these foods from the dungeon just behind my house, called the Stone Cathedral? My little friend and I would both be very grateful.
quest: I believe that Lou Ka was looking for this. Why don't you try taking it to him? I believe he stays in the bar in Shoushi.
You found them! Quick, take this to Oi-Tong Ye in town! I'm sure he will be thrilled to have it!
Oi-Tong Ye is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to him?

greetings: I have never before heard of a Drudge carrying paper! It is well known that they are far too feebleminded to understand the written word. Allow me to reward you for this fascinating discovery.
I wonder what this means? Give me a moment; I believe I may be able to translate it.

There you are. This is ... intriguing. I wish to study this more closely. In the meantime, I would like you to investigate the Mad Star more carefully. Search the nearby Crypt, if you would, and bring me anything you find.
What is this? Can this be the creature the drudges' note referred to?
Akyafi fishes a note from his pocket and reads it carefully.
No ... no ... I do not ... No, I do not know. I must study!
But thank you, friend.

If you are looking for more adventure, you might want to peruse the rumors that Jubal has at the bar. Or perhaps you should journey to Shoushi. I hear that there are many good people there who may need some help!
I am a humble scholar from Zaikhal. Of late, we have heard of the unusually large number of Drudges in the hills around the Yaraq Cove.

They seem to gather near the ruin of the Empyrean port on the far side of the cove, where the Mad Star flickers. Perhaps you could investigate, and bring me back something which would explain their presence?
I recently sent young Abmim to investigate, but he has not yet returned.
If you are having difficulty locating the Mad Star, you may buy directions from the barkeeper, Jubal. He's afraid of the Mad Star; ask him instead how to reach the Pillars of the Inner Sea.
quest: Lubziklan al-Luq was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
Hmmm? No, this isn't mine. Why don't you try asking Ma'yad about it?
Mara al-Luq is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to her?

greetings: Ah, Abmim, I knew you would one day run afoul of something. He that chooses a thief's life has it stolen from him early. My brother became a brigand and murderer, friend traveler.
Be not as foolish as he - do not lightly discard the protection this mage Asheron provides. But, as I promised, you have earned a reward.
Abmim, my brother! Ah, to learn that at the last you had renounced your evil ways! This gives me great joy and great pain - joy that you came to your sense, and pain that it came too late!
Traveler, you have eased my troubled heart. Thank you.
%n reads the scroll.
So, Ms. Kerendova needs another shipment of Enchanted Sand for hatching Armoredillos. Very well, I'll have this sent along right away.
Here, give her this invoice for the sand, so she is prepared when my delivery arrives to her.
Hail, traveler. Have you encountered a man named Abmim ibn Ibsar? He is my brother, who foolishly listened to those who whisper of an unsafe freedom to be gained in the Direlands.
We have not heard from him in several months, and begin to worry. If you bring me news of him, I would reward you as well as I may.
The last we heard, he had finally accepted some honest work from Akyafi the Translator. Perhaps Akyafi, who resides upstairs, can tell you more.
quest: Lubziklan al-Luq was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
I believe that Akyafi the Translator was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
Mara al-Luq is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to her?

greetings: Ugh... I really wish someone would teach these Shadows the use of proper paper...
Bretself shudders momentarily, and then begins to translate the lump.
Fascinating... According to this, it looks like Isin Dule is trying to stop the Raven Hand from awakening Grael. Here, take a look.
Ugh! Another of these lumps? Even worse, this ones still squirming! Still... this is fascinating.
This seems to be orders to the Shadows under Isin Dule's command. Oh my, he raised a Shadow Spire? He's ordering his forces to stop some High Archon of the Raven Hand. Here, take a look.
Hmmm... This seems to be written in some sort of Empyrean Code.
I can translate it into recognizable characters, but I can't make heads or tails of it. Seems Atlan didn't want other people reading his notes.
My apologies, but I cannot read this. It appears to be the runic script of old Dericost.  You should bring this to Kuyiza bint Zayi, in Zaikhal.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the language of the ancient Falatacot.  You should bring this to Fanzen San, in Hebian-To.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the script of old Dericost.  You should bring this to Kuyiza bint Zayi, in Zaikhal.
How interesting.... This book details Asheron's plan to defeat Bael'Zharon. Here, let me transcribe this into Roulean so that you may read it as well.
Hmm...
Oh dear... How you recovered this is beyond me, but hold on a moment, I shall give you a translation. This is quite disturbing...
This is a curious and alarming little message. It appears to be an archival record of an earlier message, sent from a garrison town to the royal court of the Empire of Yalain.

Do you realize what you have here? This appears to be nothing less than an Empyrean weapons manual! What a fabulous discovery! At long last, we have a glimpse into the lost arts of their great society.
You certainly deserve a copy a this for yourself.

Curious. This is a letter home from a soldier on campaign. A singularly disturbing campaign, if I may venture the opinion. My thanks for recovering it. We may be able to cull some valuable knowledge from this.
Here is a copy for you.
How disturbing. This scroll tells the tale of a terrible defeat suffered by the great Empyrean - and perhaps something more terrible still to she who received it so long ago.

What beautiful craftsmanship... the blossoms in the paper are still fragrant. Empyrean magic was as subtle as it was powerful. This would seem to be a journal of some sort. A moment, I shall transcribe it into Roulean.
Sweet merciful Mothers... this missive would seem to be scribed by the hand of Asheron himself! A remarkable find! I wonder what this calamity he describes was?
Revolting!  This note is written on cured human skin!  Where did you get this?  Still... here is your translation.  It was not easy, translating the language of old Dericost.
Hm. This appears to be nothing of great import. A simple request for parts from one Yalaini smith to another. Where did you say you found this?
Well, this may be of use in our researches. This is a sort of record or timeline, detailing the major events in the history of the Aerlinthe port and island.
Another of these lumps? I just got the slime off my hands from the last one.
Hm. I confess I don't understand this. Oh, I can translate it well enough, but... You say this was carried on powerful Shadows?
It's nothing like any Shadow missive I've encountered before. Usually they speak almost as we do. This is... like dark poetry. I do not understand what this message's implications are.
Where are you people finding these disgusting things? I'll never be able to eat tapioca again!
Ugh! I don't know what this is, or was, but there are letters burned into its back...
Oh. An exhortation from Bael'Zharon to his troops. Nice to know our enemies hold us in such high regard. Hmph.
Blech! I swear, the Shadows use these messenger creatures to dissuade us from reading their correspondence. They're too disgusting for most people to read!
Ugh. Watch where you hold that, young one, I don't want slime on our nice clean floor. Let me see...
Hm... A message from... How interesting.
Most interesting. It appears that the town of Xarabydun holds a treasure I would not have suspected.
My apologies, but I cannot read this. It appears to be the runic script of old Dericost. You should bring this to Kuyiza bint Zayi, in Zaikhal.
Sweet...
Mothers...
%n hands back a translation with no further word, looking stunned.
Hrm... I could be wrong, but... this seems to imply that the Lady of Ithaenc foresaw the arrival of Isparians, over two thousand years ago.
A mere scrap of ancient bureaucracy, I'm afraid. Nothing of interest to us.
What is this gibberish? I can't read it. It's just a lot of letters and numbers strung together.
What a spectacular find! I haven't encountered anything so valuable to our understanding of Empyrean magic and technology since Atlan's Treatise.
This an armor handbook for an elite order of Yalaini battle mages, completely devoted to their Emperor. Rather like our Knights of the Golden Flame, I expect.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  I couldn't even begin to be able to tell you what language this is.  Perhaps you should talk to Kuyiza bint Zayi, the translator in Zaikhal.
I am sorry, but I cannot read this.  Try talking to the Hebian-To translator, Fanzen San.
An interesting read, a bit fanatical in spot. I have made notes where they are applicable.
Will wonders never cease? This book was difficult because of the damage wrought upon it. As well the text itself was written in a variation of Dericost, akin to that of the Gelid.

I must say the first book that I translated by this author gave me pause. But this...this is a remarkably frightening man. His hatred pours onto the page. It's accentuated near the end. Also some of the secrets that are held within make me think more on Nuhmudira and her fears. It appears that they may have been well founded.
Remarkable. If you read this very carefully you may learn something about the Olthoi, and Asheron's part in their arrival here.
Disciples of Strife...a very interesting read. I've made some notes where applicable.
Disciples of Stasis...a very interesting read. I've made some notes where applicable.
Disciples of Corrosion...a very interesting read. I've made some notes where applicable.
Disciples of TEMPEST...a very interesting read. I've made some notes where applicable.
The more I read about what Gaerlan has written the more I realize that he was normal once.
I have never seen the script before, but it appears to be the same G that penned certain areas of the other books that people have brought to me lately.

This is an ancient chronicle, written in Yalaini. It is a frightening tale. If this is truth and not some fiction, there are things in this world that are best left alone to slumber in their black depths...
Looks like Harlune wasn't always an ornery old git. If I read this right he actually used to have a heart and really think he could make a difference. Hard to believe he could be so jaded.
Hard to believe... Asheron seems to be more like us than I ever thought. Real emotions, not the distant man we have come to know recently. Everything seems to weigh so heavily upon him.
The Tumerok knew about the Empyrean before who would have ever guessed. These are some interesting writings. Where did you get them again?
He didn't seem to care much for the Emperor, though he still paid him some sort of respect.
quest: This is a very pretty Empyrean bauble. The writing is largely inconsequential. I'll take care of diposing it for you, and give you what a collector might pay for it.
I am surprised I have been seeing these in circulation. Can you keep a secret?
At one point a few years ago, I was honored to receive a letter from Asheron himself, through Scholar Antius Blackmoor. I was flattered to have received it, but what he asked me was unusual.
He wished that I would watch out for anyone bearing these gems. If the person seemed powerful enough that they might know how to use them, I am to plead ignorance. I do not think you are, however

Therefore, I shall tell you - they are from a hidden cache that Asheron stored in the mountains, for use in portal creation. I am not certain precisely where he intended to open a portal to, but the gems were to be a power source. The inscription reads, simply, "Property of Asheron Realaidain," nothing more.

I shall share with you the letter I received. Perhaps it will tell you more about the gem and its uses. I'll also give you this trade note as payment for the gem - I am supposed to retain them, but I can at least offer you fair market value for them.

greetings: Fanzen San examines the collar in fascination.
This looks like Falatacot workmanship. This could be a pet's collar or something similar.

Yes, this symbol on the collar is definitely Falatacot. I believe it means "Unity". No actually this marking on the triangle represents a single person or a name. This translates better as "One of Three". Very interesting...
My my, look here, there is some writing on the inside too. Hehe, sortof a "If found please return to..." It gives a set of coordinates. Let me see...
Fanzen San opens a map of Dereth and drags his fingers along its length to rest in the Osteth Mountain range.
Yes, here it is in the Osteth Mountains. There's nothing marked there on the map, but that doesn't mean there isn't something there. The coordinates are 70.6N, 14.5W.
How disturbing! Animating timber and mineral? A curious venture.
This is a beautiful gem! Where did you say you found it? In a mud cave on the Vesayen Islands? Not surprising that the moarsmen would hoard items.

It looks almost like a portal gem. But there is something odd about it. Look at the sides of the gems. Those holes look like pegs could fit into them. Did you find anything that would fit in your journeys?

Either way, I can tell this item has some significance. I won't keep it from you, just seeing it was enough to tantalize my imagination. Whether you crush it and open a portal with it now, or hold on to it is wholly up to you.
This is a beautiful looking emerald trinket. How do I know it is made of Emerald? Just because I am cooped up in here doesn't mean I don't know how to use an ust.

This clasp looks like it is hinged, and it has a pair of carved pegs. This was pulled from some muck you say? Others have come by to show me a gem that they recovered that this artifact may very well fit around. I suggest you find one if you can and see if it fits.
Hmmm... as I think about it, this object may also have the makings of an interesting piece of jewelry. If only you had the right kind of string, perhaps you might be able to make it wearable.

What a remarkable finding! This appears to be a cradle for some sort of item. I recall in my travels of Ispar that the Aluvians would make similar objects to place curious or small decorative statues into.

Several people have visited me recently with an object that could very well be placed in this. They said they made the gem by combining a pair of items they found on the Vesayen Islands. I recommend exploring the islands further if you haven't already.

The stone glows, but it looks very fragile. I wonder if it could be powdered and if the powder could be used to enchant a piece of jewelry. But don't take my word for it. What you do with this artifact is your decision and not mine.
This is an interesting structure. A dais made out of jade! Look at the top of it, there are several indentations. This was likely used as a dais for a statue of some sort.

Now that I think of it, several people have come by with a piece of artwork that may very well fit on top of this. They said they got that item from somewhere on the Vesayen Islands, though they were very secretive about where it was they pulled their treasure from.

Another thing to note is the weight and sound of the dais. It feels very light for being make out of stone, and it sounds like it could be hollow. I see no hinges or doors, perhaps you should take this to Hiro outside of Xarabydun, he may know how to open this casing.
But don't take my word for it. Either keep it or take it to Hiro. The choice is yours.
My apologies, but I cannot read this. Kuyiza bint Zayi, one of the scholars of Zaikhal, would be able to assist you.
An interesting page to translate. The text is Falatacot, but of a different dialect. Very strange.
A pity the whole story isn't here. I'd be fascinated to see if there are any differences in their lore.
A most fascinating text. The bulk of it seems to be focused around something called "The Spear of Mukkir" and its interactions with the Falatacot.
I recall overhearing something in the pub about a fellow named Sarkin Killcrane investigating a connection between the shadows and this Spear of Mukkir. I believe he is stationed in Wai Jhou.
Oh! I nearly forgot, here's the translation. Pardon my absent mindedness. Getting my hands on a text as old as this is a treat. I tend to get distracted by such opportunities.
Fanzen San chuckles.
Ah, I fear this text is not of my ken.  This is written in the runes of Dericost, a later civilization.  Kuyiza bint Zayi, one of the scholars of Zaikhal, would be able to assist you.

Indeed, this is the ancient cuneiform of the Falatacot. However, it does not seem to be contemporaneous. If I read this correctly, the text written at a far later period, possibly as late as the High Empyrean Era of Lore.
How curious. Who would be using such an obscure language at so late a date, and why?
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the script of ancient Empyrea.  You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
Hmm.... Now let's see....
This isn't a good sign at all. If what this says is true. Oh my. See for yourself.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the script used by the High Empyrean culture of the Age of Lore.  You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
Interesting find... The language of old Dericost is difficult to translate, but I believe I can do it.  What is this strange material?
My apologies, but I cannot read this. It appears to be the script used by the High Empyrean culture of the Age of Lore. You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
Ah, I fear this text is not of my ken.  This is written in the runes of Dericost, a later civilization. Kuyiza bint Zayi, one of the scholars of Zaikhal, would be able to assist you.
Revolting! What is this abomination?
No, never mind. I do not wish to know. Take it to Bretslef, in Cragstone.
Hrm. Well, the letters of this are in the High Empyrean language of the Age of Lore. However, they don't seem to form any words.
Interesting!  These letters seem to reference some of the events that recently occurred here in Dereth.  Judging by the end of the notes, I wonder if the author is still alive...
I am sorry, but I cannot read this.  Try talking to the Zaikhal translator, Kuyiza bint Zayi.
An interesting read, a bit fanatical in spot. I have made notes where they are applicable.
Will wonders never cease? This book was difficult because of the damage wrought upon it. As well the text itself was written in a variation of Dericost, akin to that of the Gelid.
I must apologize. The book... well the book... well it... well... here are my notes. I'm truly sorry.

This appears to be Falatacot in nature, but the language is older. I'm not familiar with the dialect, though some words appear to be very close with many of the writings that I have translated in the past.
Here, I translated as much as I could. I find it rather disturbing.
This is the Faltacot command for open. That is strange.
Ah! I see you have found my note. I asked the barkeeps on the Vesayen Islands to distribute it for me. And since you are here, giving this to me, it appears they did what I had asked.

With all that has been happening of late I can't help but be intrigued by all of this Falatacot nonsense. So far we've seen a good deal about the under handed side of their people. But we know there is a lighter side to them. A less cruel side.

We also know that the Moarsmen, the swamp dwelling creatures that were discovered when portals to the Vesayen Islands first opened, have some sort of connection to them. The Adjanites frequently kept them, though we are not exactly certain why.
I would enjoy the opportunity to learn more about them, but I honestly have very little time outside of my translator duties to devote to researching the moarsmen.
I know! Since you are here, would you mind going back to the Vesayen Islands and look for information for me? I can't leave this building, but I can read as much as I want!

This book appears to be a text regarding the eating habits of the Moarsmen and some creature call the Moars. I am unfamiliar with what the Moar are exactly, but it seems there is some relation between them and the Moarsmen.
Unfortunately, the text is in horrible condition and I am unable to translate it completely. The best I can do is create a summary of the bits I understand.
Since you have helped me further my understanding of the Moarsmen and the Falatacot, I will help you.

This book appears to be a text regarding the hunting habits of the Moarsmen and what seems to be their less advance counterparts, the Moar. The text claims them to be vicious hunters, always on the roam.

The years have not been kind to this text. There are so many pages that I simply cannot comprehend because of their poor condition. The best I can do for this tome is to create a summary of the legible bits.

Finally! Something with substance. As much as I enjoyed reading about the Moarsmen, those tomes pale compared to this one. This looks to be a history of the Moarsmen on Dereth. Hmm... this also seems to only be one part of the history. A second tome may contain the conclusion of the account.
Sadly, the pages dissolve as I attempt to read them, so I was only able to construct a high level summary. The finer details of the text were gone before I could transcribe them.
quest: Ah, another copy of the book you found in the Faltacot's Meeting Place. Thank you, I may be able to find more clues :about the High Matriarch in this.
I never knew that Aquamarine could be such a prismatic gem. I always thought it was opaque.

None the less, this is an interesting Adjanite Artifact, to be certain. Though I cannot say for certain what it is exactly. My library on the Adjanites is thin in comparison to what I have regarding the Falatacot.
I do recall, though, that some adventurers can come across a device that these gems could be fitted into.

You may want to return to the Vesayen Islands and search for that contraption. . I did, at one point, possess an interesting cutting tool. Alas, I have already given it away. Come back to me in a few days and I might have found another one.
But what you do if completely up to your decision.
Fanzen San looks over the scroll, growing alarm in his features.
How many of these are there?  Well, again, thank you for bringing it to me.  Unfortunately, I have nothing to give you this time...
This High Matriarch, this "One of Three", must have sent the burun messenger you intercepted.
She may have something to do with the other recent Falatacot activities I've heard about. I may send a message to the Royal Guard concerning this. Thank you for your help friend.
You may want to return to the Vesayen Islands and search for that contraption. If you don't, I found an interesting cutting tool that you could use to break this cluster of prisms from each other.
But what you do is completely up to your decision.
Fanzen San looks over the scroll, with a concerned look on his face.

This is a scroll detailing how to summon a creature known as a Dark Inferno, a shadow twisted manifestation of the element of fire.  It is good that you brought this to me, for I fear the repercussions were someone else to retrieve it.  You are a stalwart adventurer, so I will share some of the knowledge imparted upon me by some of the translated Falatacot texts I have discovered.
He traces a glyph in the air, and you feel light-headed.
You have gained 3 points of Magic Defense skill!

greetings: My apologies, but I cannot read this.  You should bring this to Fanzen San, in Hebian-To.

The undead General who wrote this book seems to be very deeply involved in Emperor Geraine's plans. As you'll see, the information is disturbing, but may be the key needed to thwart whatever it is Emperor Geraine is up to.
There you are.  This was gained from a powerful Revenant you say?  He would appear to have been several millenia old!  I wonder if there are others of his antiquity still walking Dereth?
I translated this best I could, but the level of complexity in this research is impressive.
There is, however, one part that may point to this factory they speak of. Perhaps Sir Donovan can make use of it to track it down.
Here you go. Good luck
Well, this explains a lot, and raises even more questions. I did not think the plight of the Empyreans was related to the actions of Emperor Geraine, but I guess it was.
There's a Royal Investigator, Sir Daeglan, I believe his name is, that was researching any information he could find on Emperor Geraine's actions. He may well be interested in this.
Last I heard, he was in the camp next to the Lost City of Neftet, researching the ritual site that was uncovered there.
This has to be one of the more disturbing tomes I have ever transcribed. If it is true, then there truly is no telling what Emperor Geraine is capable of.
My apologies. There is very little in this tome, as the last of it is damaged. I recovered what I could.
This seems to be some sort of report about those strange Bloodstones I've heard about, up by the Gurogs.
There's one of Borelean's Royal Knights, Sir Donovan, who was doing research on the Bloodstones. I'd bet he'd be interested in this.
Last I heard, he was up at the encampment along the borders of the Gurog's frozen valley. You should be able to find him there.
Indeed, this is the runic script of old Dericost, a language not used in well over 5000 years.  A moment - I shall transcribe a copy for you into Roulean.
Hm. This appears to be a portalspace coordinate. Such things are not within my knowledge. You might want to seek out my colleague Marisa bint Fuya.
She would be able to cast a portal to this location. Unfortunately, she's on sabbatical, and has gone to the town of Plateau.
Be warned, though - you will need a substantial party to reach the Lost City, and should you die...
You will be unable to reenter the caves to recover your equipment. Be certain you are prepared before you ask Mairisa to cast the portal!

Ah, but this is not the language of Dericost.  Do you see the sharp, triangular shapes the characters are composed of? This is almost certainly the written word of the Falatacot, a far older, and far less understood culture.
Fanzen San, in Hebian-To, would be able to translate this for you.
I can indeed translate this for you into Roulean.
This is... fascinating. This work seems to explain what the Gelidites were doing in their long exile.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the script of ancient Empyrea.  You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the language of the ancient Falatacot.  You should bring this to Fanzen San, in Hebian-To.
Oh dear...
This doesn't bode well. No, not at all. Take a look for yourself.

I fear I cannot help you with this. You see that this writing style is like our own? It appears to be the script used by the High Empyrean culture of the Age of Lore. My specialty is the runic language of Dericost. You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
This note seems to be written on cured skin... Not human skin, but something similar.  The contents of the note are quite disturbing, and written in an archaic dialect of ancient Dericostian.
Aerfalle... I have seen this name before. An adventurer brought me a note from Rytheran, the Revenant of the Mage Academy near Mount Esper. It was addressed to an Aerfalle. But this... a moment...
Heavens and earth! This speaks of the last Shadow War, and in grave detail. I am... profoundly disturbed by the sights this Aerfalle has witnessed.
Ew! What IS that?
Take it to Bretslef in Cragstone. I don't want to touch it!
%n grabs a flask of water and hurriedly scrubs her hands.
Ah yes, this is interesting. This came from a Mu-Miyah, you say. Curious. This would seem to be some sort of memoir.
I wonder what would provoke such soul searching? Although I have noted that the undead seem prone to rambling reminiscence... I suppose when one is that old, it becomes inevitable.
This is most intriguing! It would seem we have have allies in our war against the forces of Bael'Zharon. Of a sort, anyway.
This is useful. There is an army of undead gathering somewhere in the wilderness. Odd that they have not been seen yet.
It would seem they do not all get along. Old grudges, I suppose.
Heavens and earth, do you know what this is? This is nothing less than the undeads' own analysis of the Shadows' activity.
I have little doubt that this information will be invaluable in the near future. You may have given us a crucial edge.
Your pardon, but I must leave soon to confer with my colleagues and the Consortium of Archmages...
Hm, interesting. Looks like you caught this monster in the middle of writing a report to its superior.
Well. This undead certainly thinks the world owes her. I can't imagine how obnoxious she'd be in person. If there's anything worse than a smelly abomination, it's a smarmy smelly abomination.
Magnificent! The dates in this journal stretch back to the last Shadow War. What an invaluable asset to our studies! It will take some time to go over this thoroughly. Here are the last few entries.
Ah, yes, this appears to be a unique teleport spell. Give me a moment, and I can teach it to you.
Hrm. Well, the letters of this are in the High Empyrean language of the Age of Lore. However, they don't seem to form any words.
I do not recognize this language at all... Try talking to Diyas al-Yat, here in Zaikhal.  He's an odd man who spends his time studying the Virindi.
What is this?  Perhaps Diyas could make some sense of it...
I am sorry, but I cannot read this.  Try talking to the Hebian-To translator, Fanzen San.
An interesting read, a bit fanatical in spot. I have made notes where they are applicable.
Will wonders never cease? This book was difficult because of the damage wrought upon it. As well the text itself was written in a variation of Dericost, akin to that of the Gelid.
This is a personal missive, written very recently. I'd be interested to see if there were more like it.
A second note written in the same hand, and like the first a missive written recently. What are they working on?
The World Shaper. I wonder what that title means? Keep bringing these to me as you find them, please.
Well it appears that these letters are beginning to take on a more active ken. I'd be interested in seeing if there were anymore.
This must be the last of them. It has an air of finality to it. I wonder what sacrifice the writer is speaking about.
Kuyiza begins translating and transcribing the text for you, happily chatting along as she works.
It has been such a long while since I have had something new to work with. People usually bring me bits of parchment from Frore... not that I mind Frore...
Sometimes they bring me something about the undead scholar Rytheran... but I've seen most of what is said in those texts already...
Wonderful!  Can you see the portal energy pulsing within it?
No doubt you have seen and experienced much on this adventure!
I have heard stories that the ancient dead of Dereth talk to each other as we do, and form a society underneath our own...
Let us see where this Kelannik fellow liked to travel.
Why, I do believe that this portal leads to the Mage Academy!  Beware young traveler, this place is not for the faint of heart...
What a magnificent artifact to behold. I thought this item was destroyed ages ago.
I must reward you greatly for this surprise gift!
Have you any news of my old colleague Celcynd, of Rithwic?  I have not seen him in many years, and I do fear for his peace of mind.
Hail, traveler. It is pleasant to meet anyone here in the wastes.  Tell me, have you discovered a crypt in these regions called the Burial Temple?
I have heard that the dead walk there, and one in particular always carries a certain black gem I seek for my research.
Through my studies, I have found that the dreadful creature is named Kelannik.
Please retrieve this gem and return it to me.  Your courage will not go unrewarded.
Well, Jourgensson says you're all right.  Maybe you can help.  Down underneath the castle, there's a prison full of beasties.  That idiot Gwillim dropped some notes and his bag in there.
Now he says he can't mix potions!  Bring the bag back to him, and he'll reward you.  You'll need this to get in there.

Errukh! A letter from my long-lost cousin, MacNiall! Arrr, it's good to see the old boy doing well! I ought to reward ye for this, as he says. Here then, have one of my blade hilts. I'm workin' on a way to improve daggers and light swords.
Arrr!  Don't bother me!  I've got enough problems on me hands!  Talk to my lieutenant, Jourgensson!
Yes, I can provide transit to the location written here. I believe you will have need of this.  A passing adventurer threw it at my head some time ago, when my portal spell fizzled.
It can't be I thought this had been lost long ago....
Mairisa slowly opens the box, the golden glow washes across her face. Her facial expression seems to become more calm.
Thank you kind adventurer, it was a kind gesture of yours to return this to it's rightful owner.
I came here to be free of the madding pace of the Arcanum at Zaikhal. Unless you have urgent business, I'd prefer to be left to my meditation.

If you are another seeking the lost City of Frore, be warned - you will need a substantial party to survive. Should you die, you will be unable to reenter the caves to recover your equipment. Be certain you are prepared.
What a pretty piece of shell! But I can't do anything with it. Sorry.
What a pretty, and large, piece of shell! I'm afraid I haven't the faintest idea what to do with it, though.
This is a beautiful pearl! You should match your wardrobe around it!
How disgusting!
There is, however, a sage somewhere in the southern mountain range that actually likes those things. How revolting...
This is a nice shiny bauble! I can't do anything with it though. Maybe one of the outlaws in Bandit Castle can help you.
That is a fine robe, indeed.
I can take the hides of certain creatures and turn them into items of value.
Have you the skins of armoredillos, gromnies, or reedsharks?    I can use them in my craft.
Yo-Jin holds the robe up reverently and looks a bit nervous.
Good thing I left enough here to make alterations... I'll just be a moment.
Whew, here you go. It'll fit over other armor pieces now.
Here you go. People have been telling me about a strange new plant that's been found in some dungeons and around the landscape. Quite a colorful thing, or so they say.
Here's your armor! I overheard someone talking about the new plants again. They sound so lovely! I'll bet someone with the proper skills could crush them up and make a fine dye.
Enjoy the armor! May it keep the burn off your back. Oh my! The plants are just all I can think about... It's a pity that I can't use them in my craft due to all the harsh chemicals I use.
I never thought I could make such a sturdy hide into a fine shirt like this! I hope it's not to scratchy on your skin!
Here you go!
I find greaves so aesthetically pleasing. Even if they do come from those brutish reedsharks. Perchance have you tried dyeing your other pieces of armor?
A friend gave me a dyeing pot, but I don't seem to be able to dye any of the leather armor I craft from creature hides.
Reedsharks have such rough, ugly skin. Crafting from their skin always punishes my delicate hands!
By the way, have you tried dyeing armor yet? Try as I might, I just can't seem to get the knack of it!
Ah, another masterpiece! Such a drab, gray color though. It's quite a shame that I have to apply so many chemicals to treat the leather, otherwise they could be infused with such color!
It pains my heart to make such dowdy-colored armor. A pity this cannot be dyed.
Have you tried dyeing any other armor yet? Be careful... if you do a poor job you might damage your armor, and that would certainly be dreadful!
Wow, this thing reminds me of those strange Hoary Mattekar hides. Only, not as hoary, or protective, for that matter. But there is more material here to work with...
This is rather exotic! It is sort of a claw shield.
A Mattekar claw?  I don't think I can make clothing out of this one.  Well, here, have this.

Yes, the Hoary Mattekars are now back. Given the strangeness of creature migrations that have occurred over this past year, I would not be surprised were the Hoary to be a more permanent fixture on Dereth.    Here is your robe.
Yes, there's enough material here for me to let this out a bit... Very well, I'll just be a moment.
There you go. It'll fit over other armor pieces now.
Oh my! Will you just look at this drab old thing! I'll spruce it up for you and make you the star you were meant to be!
What's this? Warmer than the Hoary that is for sure. Hmm... This seems to be a mattekar who has adapted to a warmer climate. Interesting.
The hide is a little tougher, though not meant for the cold. Against heat however, this should do quite nicely.
The little shreths are kind of cute, aren't they? It is a pity that people have found a way to use their skin. Now they will be hunted like most of the other poor creatures of Dereth.
Some of the larger shreths are just coming into their own. They are aggressive not out of hostility, but out of fear. Killing them is not the answer!
In killing the shreth of today, we may be dooming our tomorrow. Perhaps the shreths hold an answer to an unforeseen plague, or some equally monumental task. I urge you to reconsider hunting them!
This probably came from a baby ursuin somewhere... Loincloths are so last year.
Ursuin make wonderful garments! Their coats make lovely coats that are functional too! Of course I can make a mattekar coat look even better than an ursuin one...
This is a pretty small shank of hide.  But never fear, Yi Yo Jin has never failed at making something both fashionable, and affordable!
Wow! Ursuin hides are so soft in the spring and summer season! Maybe I'll take the extra strips from your coat and line my breeches with them...
This tooth would make a fine implement of destruction. Take it, and strike down my enemies!
Ursuins certainly have large heads. Personally, I like their coats better than these helms.
This has just the splash of color that you'll need to really shine like a star!
Remember, snakeskin is like make-up.  Too much and it makes you look like a tawdry matron!
This helmet is nice because it goes with anything that you wear. Sclavus are so useful when they die.
This is large enough to craft into a well fitting cuirass I think.
Well then. I think that this may be the first of a great many new robes to come my friend. Make sure to show your friends.
Not quite as sturdy as the tanned red hide that I worked with before, but it's still strong enough and large enough to craft into a nice robe. Wear it well.
Let's see. The hide is thick and leathery, and aside from the small bony protrusions it's in fine shape. I think a nice set of leggings.
There you go.
Another fine specimen. A little thicker than the last shreth hide I was given to work with. Let me have a moment and I'll... Yes, yes that's it!
Here you go.
Where did you get this? It's rather frightening, and rancid smelling. Well, let me see what I can do with it.
I've seen something like this recently. Came from a carenzi though, it mottled and smelled rank. Much like this. Where are you finding these creatures?
Well, I've done the best I can.
What is this!? I've never seen anything like this. It will make a fine robe I think. Give me a moment.
Yes, there it is done.
I've seen some interesting hides pass my way, but the hides that people have been bringing me most recently are the oddest.
A few more threads...and done!
Be careful out there.
quest: Yo-Jin holds the hide up reverently and looks a bit scared.
Well, I have Kresovus' permission to craft this hide now, but I'm still not sure I want to. You must be pretty important for Kresovus to allow this.
Yo-Jin hesitates and then begins his work, deftly cutting Balor's hide in the pattern for a robe.

Here you are. I don't mind saying that this is some of my best work. Be careful with this, I'm not sure Kresovus would be so giving if you let it come to harm. Oh, and be tactful, don't wear this around Kresovus.
Yi Yo-Jin rubs the fur between his fingers and peers closely at it.
This is a rather unusual Mattekar hide. Hmm, the last time I saw fur like this was when I visited Linvak Tu...
No, No, No! I am not going to be responsible for making a robe out of this hide.
What are you doing, trying to get me killed?

greetings: So. You are a competent warrior. You may be strong enough to suit my purposes. My father resides in the Mountain Fortress, well south of Qalaba'r. I am... concerned for his well-being.
Please bring this letter to him. If you bring me back a letter from him, I will reward you. You will also need this key to reach him.  Do not go to find him if you fear the darkness.
Thank you. This is what I needed to know.
Take this as my thanks. It was given to me by a master assassin dressed in green armor. Please... leave me now. I have much to think on.
I have slain others for speaking to me without a proper introduction.
Oh no! You have to find Dansha-Ki and give this to her, otherwise there is no hope in seeing her return. Please hurry!

Can you help me? My sister went south headed towards Dryreach for some much needed supplies. She has not returned and I fear the Tumeroks may have captured her again. Kind soul, can you help find her for me?  I'm really worried for her safety.
However, I can't just send anyone to rescue her. Bring me an insignia from a Tumerok to prove your strength. Then I'll trust you in saving my sister.
quest: I'm sorry, I can't possibly impose on you to rescue my sister again. But, if you find someone worthy, send them my way...

Perhaps you can help me! My sister was last seen near the outskirts of Dryreach. Please find her for me. Time is of the essence! I'll give you thirty minutes to save her, otherwise I'll have to find her myself and hope I alone can rescue her.

greetings: Oh, thank you most sincerely. I have been quite distraught over its loss but have been unable to retrieve it myself. Take this moonstone as a token of my gratitude.

Perhaps you can assist me. I am known as Miyako, the poet. I left a precious volume of my poetry in some pretty tunnels east of here when I was searching for inspiration. Were you to return the poems to me, I would reward you.
Thank you, I'm conducting some experiments on motes. Are you working on the formulas for the new spells? How many tapers are you using? You may not need as many as you think...
Thank you, this will be useful. Are you researching those new War Magic spells? Have you tried replacing a taper with a scarab?
Thank you. In my travels, a powerful mage told me how to rid oneself of unwanted enchantments. Unfortunately, in the process the caster is also stripped of his beneficial spells.
Thank you. I've received some new information that's allowing me to brew potions to counteract enchantments placed upon the imbiber.
A sliver of pyreal, excellent.  If you're interested in learning the new War Magic spells, I know they use the talisman of old. I just forget which property of the spell that affects...
A pyreal sliver, how generous of you! While researching the new War Magic spells, I found the herb used in the slow moving wall spells has its ties in the realms of portal magic.
A sliver? I can certainly use this! As far as I can tell, the herb used in the ring spells is used nowhere else.
Excellent, a sliver! Thankfully, I did not need to smelt any new alchemical substances to determine the elements of the new War Magic spells.
A fine sliver! There are new counter-magics being found! The current research indicates that to use these spells, the counter spell must be a full order above the unwanted spell.
An excellent piece of pyreal! Thank you. I've been thinking a great deal about these 'dispels' and how they relate to the newly discovered war magics.
I'm not sure, but I don't think the dispels are using only diamond scarabs.
It's a tiny one... but it's definitely a sliver of pyreal. I think I've finally realized what's happening with the new anti-magic spells.
They use two scarabs, the first is used to focus the spell down to the power of the unwanted spells and the second is a powerful scarab used to amass the energies for the countereffects.
Ooh, a fine sliver, indeed. It's become obvious in my research that I need to lean on the negative properties of the components.
Apparently whomever discovered these spells thought that getting rid of enchantments was a bad thing.

Ahh, a nugget of pyreal! Thank you. As a sign of gratitude, take these scarabs. I no longer need many since I've researched the new spells and they seem to burn far less once I was actually able to cast the spells.

Ooh, I always forget how heavy an entire bar is. Thank you. With all of my spell research done, I've taken to writing down the formulas on scrolls. Here, take this scroll, I hope you can learn from it.

I see that K'rank is still interested in keeping our deal running. Well, tell him that I am still willing to uphold my end of the bargain. Not long ago, I even saw the blood witch talking to Olcris, making sure that he was well taken care of I assume. She makes me uneasy when she is around. Oh, there's more, but that is left for Captain K'rank to report on.
I'll be looking forward to the next delivery.
I trade in rare metals and information. I am only interested in motes from golems and the new ore the Lugians have been mining.
If you bring me motes, slivers, nuggets and bars of pyreal, I will share some of my knowledge with you.
quest: Ah, a piece of that new ore. I'll wager you had to dodge a lot of Lugians to get this! Let me purify it for you. Good luck finding someone to smith it, though.
This is that chorizite, then, is it? Peculiar stuff... The medium grade you have here is too brittle to forge, but it does break up easily.
This is the very purest grade of chorizite. You must be formidable to have survived in the mines of the Lugians. I don't know of any smiths with a forge hot enough to shape it, though.
I'm sorry, I really don't have the supplies to purify metals for you right now. Please come back later, as I hope to be getting more in soon.

greetings: This is beneath my capabilities. Take it back.
I can do nothing with this.  I can make arrowheads out of the smaller crystal pieces, but not pieces of this size.
There was something strange going on in Uziz. If my brothers and I weren't so busy mastering our craft we could have done some snooping around. On to greener pastures though as Gerloc always says.

This gem must surely be unique! Take this bow, imbued with the unique essence of the soul crystal. Such a powerful bow can only fire arrows with a special head. If you bring me shards from crystal fragments, I can make such arrowheads for you. And beware! If you lose this bow, it is gone forever.
If you prefer crossbows, you will have to find some way to attach it to a stock.

A unique soul crystal gem! Take this bow, imbued with the gem's power. It will only fire arrows with heads which I can craft for you, so bring me crystal shards and I will make arrowheads for you. This bow is completely unique, however, and irreplaceable if lost.
If you need a crossbow, you must attach it to a stock yourself.

A unique gem, filled with power! Impressive. Here is your gem-infused bow. Such a bow can only fire arrows made with crystal arrowheads. Bring me crystal fragments and I will make you such arrowheads. A word of warning: this bow is irreplaceable! Lose it and you will never again see its like.
If you want a crossbow, you must attach the stock yourself.

A rare and powerful gem. Here is your bow, infused with the crystal's essence. Remember that this bow can only fire ammunition made from crystal fragments, which I can make for you if you give me crystal shards. I am sure you appreciate how rare the gems are, so take care not to lose your bow!
If you desire a crossbow, you must attach it to a stock yourself. If you desire an atlatl, give me back the bow and I'll see what I can do.
I've also taken the liberty of granting you some practical knowledge...

A rare gem, of considerable power. Take this bow, infused with the gem's energy. Remember, the bow can only fire crystal-tipped arrows. I can make appropriate arrowheads for you if you give me crystal shards. You must be aware of the rarity of these gems, so do not lose your bow! You may not be able to find another.
If you wish to have a crossbow, I cannot help you. You must fit a stock to it yourself. If you wish an atlatl, give me back the bow and I'll see what I can do.

A wondrous gem, a miracle of rare device! Here is a bow, equally rare and precious and irreplaceable. The bow will only fire crystal-tipped ammunition, so bring me crystal shards and I will make arrowheads for you.
If you need a crossbow, you must find a way to fit a stock yourself. If you need an atlatl, give me back the bow and I'll see what I can do.
Excellent, I assume you seek crystal ammunition. Take these crystal arrowheads.
Seeking ammunition, are you? I hope you enjoy using that bow I made. Or are you a crossbow user? In any case... here are your crystal arrowheads.
A shard of this size makes for a sizable number of arrowheads! Here are your arrowheads.
Well, it's no bow, but I do have this old contraption here. Remember, this can only fire crystal-tipped darts.
Look at this! I haven't seen one of these antiques in a while! Here, let me improve it for you.

If you can find a gem more powerful than a mere scintillating gem, I would be interested in it. Give me such a gem and I will use it to craft a magical bow for you. The bow will be so powerful, in fact, that normal ammunition will not work on it. You will have to come to me for arrowheads as well. If you have one my old missile weapons, I will improve it for you.
I am not a crossbow maker, however, so if you need a crossbow you will have to attach a stock to the bow yourself.
This is beneath my capabilities. Take it back.
I am going to miss Uziz. I won't miss the townsfolk though. They sure have been acting creepy lately.
This powerful gem allows me to make you a unique spellcasting orb! The orb is irreplaceable, mind you, so take care not to misplace it!
A noteworthy gem. I can imbue a spellcasting orb with its power. But this orb, unique as it is, cannot be replaced if lost, so be very very careful with it!

The power in this gem makes me shiver. The orb I have made for you will never be equaled. But its power also makes it irreplaceable! So if you lose it, do not come back to me expecting a replacement. Sometimes life can be cruel.
A rare gem of some power. Here is an orb infused with its essence. Remember, this orb will be difficult if not impossible to replace, so be careful with it!
I've also taken the liberty of granting you some practical knowledge...
This gem holds a respectable amount of crystal essence. Take this orb as your just reward for your effort. But be careful with it, as you may not ever be able to replace it if you lose it!
As powerful an orb as I have ever seen, with one exception... Here is an orb of equal power and rarity. Remember, if you lose this orb, I will not be able to replace it for you!
Look at this! I think there's even a crack in it! Let me shine it up for you.
I have heard of powerful gems, more powerful than the mediocre gems you bring to those so-called master smiths. If I had such a gem, I could make a powerful spell-casting orb with unique properties.
Of course, if you are not a masterful mage, you should speak with one of my younger brothers. If you have one of my old orbs, I will improve it for you.
This is beneath my capabilities. Take it back.
Those folks in Uziz sure were acting...odd. It was time for a change of scenery anyways.
A powerful gem, but only barely worth my attention. Here is a shield for you. Be very careful with it, as it is quite valuable and irreplaceable. You will never find its like again.
A noteworthy gem indeed. Here is a powerful shield imbued with its essence. Be careful. This shield is unique and cannot be replaced.

A gem of unmatched power! I salute your ability. Take this shield to protect yourself in battle, worthy warrior. But take heed, there will never be another shield equal to this. It cannot be replaced! So as it protects you, so must you protect it.
Impressive achievement, finding this gem. Allow me to infuse a shield with its essence. Take good care of this shield, as I doubt you will be able to find another such gem.
I've also taken the liberty of granting you some practical knowledge...
A worthy gem. It allows me to craft a powerful shield. May this shield protect you well in the days ahead. But take care with it! It will not be easily replaced!
Most impressive. This gem allows me to craft a shield of exceptional power. Wear it proudly in battle. But all worthy things are rare... So take care not to lose this shield!
This old thing? Why, I can make it so much better for you.

Greetings. My siblings and I traveled here seeking gems of great power. I hear that there are some master armorers who craft suits of armor from fused gems. Those are beneath my notice. Bring me something even more powerful than a scintillating gem, and I will craft a great and unique shield for you. If you have one of my old shields, I will improve it for you.
Diyas stares into the fragment of crystal for a moment, and he spends a long time seeming to sort through everything he's learning.

Ah, so Felizio sent you to get something translated. I don't trust that one myself, but the invasion of Gharu'n by the blue-skinned dogs was a fresh wound in my heart when I first came here. Still, he works for the Arcanum, and on this world, Isparian differences are best put aside...

This is simply fascinating. Not only are these Apostate Virindi trying to construct their own New Singularity, but they are experimenting in strange and unpredictable elements, like this Aetherium ore. Well, I could go on all day about what's in this note, but maybe you should get it to Felizio as soon as you can.
Isn't it lovely? I do so like the Virindi countenance.
No, no -- you keep that! It's a work of art!
No, no thank you. I don't like the feel of this one.
Diyas al-Yat shivers.
You might try that ... Virindi ... in Yanshi.
Ugh. I don't want that!
No, no thank you. I don't like the feel of this one. And Leopold won't take it either.
Interesting. I've never seen a Virindi crystal quite like this.
As Diyas gazes into the Message Shard a horrified look washes over his face.
The message encoded within is quite disturbing. I have translated it as best I could, but much of the message I was unable to comprehend.
Interesting...very interesting.
Diyas grasps the Shard tightly. Suddenly he shrieks in pain and drops the Message Shard to the ground.

Did I say interesting? I meant disturbing. Disturbing and painful! It was almost as if I could feel the emotions of whatever twisted creature compiled this shard. Take this, it was the best I was able to do.
You need something translated? Let's see what we have here...
Diyas stares into the crystal for a moment. He looks puzzled as he hands a note to you.
A strange piece of writing, but little surprises me with the Virindi these days.
Another Virindi crystal? Fantastic!
Those Virindi with their tests and their experiments. Why can't we all just get along?
I never tire of translating the soapbox ramblings of the arrogant Virindi.
Diyas looks into the Fractured Message Shard. He quickly writes on a parchment and places it into your pack.
Surprise, surprise. Another Virindi with a serious superiority complex.
I heard that Aruq sent you off to that new fortress in the Direlands. Is this the shard you found there? Fascinating... Let me have a look...
Diyas stares into the fragment of crystal for a moment, and his eyes widen with horror.
The Virindi rebels are gathering their allies again! They seek to step into the gap left by T'thuun's defeat! Quick, take this translation to Aruq, he will make sure the proper people are notified.
Well, this is disturbing...
These Tanada from the House of Water seem to have become the pawns of forces greater than themselves. Here, have a look for yourself.
Ah, a message shard from a Virindi Consul found in the southern land bridge? Most intriguing... Let me see if I can translate it for you...
A strange, cold light emanates from the eyes of Diyas al-Yat as he concentrates on the message shard.

I have translated the shard for you. You should bring that translation to Meshenq. He will know what to do with such dire news. Imagine, Nanjou Shou-Jen corrupted by the chaos Virindi! Such an abomination!

Also, Meshenq has told me he gave you a medallion he took from the Tanada who attacked him. The medallion is attuned to the corrupted spirits of the House of Water Tanada. If you give it to me, I can channel its magic to make it useful to you, but I am afraid it will lose the property that grants you access to the House of Water.
